docs.title: Ferry
docs.text:
Code-first schema and safe content deployment for Umbraco 17.

Ferry keeps schema in your code and moves content between sites, such as development, staging and live:

  • Code-first schema. SchemaBuilder lets you state data types, templates, media types and document types in ordinary Umbraco migrations. Each migration runs once per environment and is reviewed like any other code. Keys are derived from aliases, so every environment gets identical schema. An existing site can adopt code-first by downloading its schema as one migration that keeps every key. See code-first schema.
  • Content-only sites. With Ferry:Full:ContentOnly set, a site accepts content and rejects any transfer that would change its schema, and the error lists what to deploy first.
  • Reviewed transfers. Send and Get (Push and Pull in the API) show a summary and every create, update and move before anything is applied, and nothing is applied without an owner-bound approval. Schema, media files, references and blocks travel with the content.
  • Deployment workflow. A per-user transfer queue, offline .csync.zip packages, import at startup, snapshots and restore points, and Umbraco user-group permissions for delegated editors.
  • Schema as generated migrations. Schema edits in the development backoffice become C# migrations you commit; every environment runs the ones it is missing at startup and reports drift. See generated migrations.
  • Extensible. Custom property editors and package data (Skybrud redirects, Umbraco Forms, or your own package) can join transfers. See extending Ferry.
  • Safe on real sites. One operation runs at a time across load-balanced instances (database lease). Indexing and caches pause during large imports. Each apply writes a recovery journal.

Documentation: https://imkeuri.github.io/ferry-umbraco/

Ferry is a self-contained package: it needs no other synchronisation tool or file export.

Free to use, closed source. Ferry is free for any site, including commercial work, under the Ferry Freeware License; its source is not published.

Status: experimental, pre-1.0. Tested on Umbraco 17.6.2 and .NET 10. See supported scope for exactly what is verified and the validation record for evidence.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
dotnet add package Ferry.Umbraco
dotnet add package Ferry.Backoffice

builder.CreateUmbracoBuilder()
    .AddBackOffice()
    .AddWebsite()
    .AddComposers()
    .AddFerryUmbracoFull()
    .Build();

Configuration lives under a Ferry section in appsettings.json; Host integration covers transport, connections and options.

docs.title: Using the backoffice
docs.text:
Ferry.Backoffice adds a Ferry workspace under Settings › Synchronisation:

Tab What it is for Overview Your connected sites and their last activity, Send to another site and Get from another site (whole site or chosen pages), and recent activity. With no site connected it offers Connect your first site. Sites Connected sites with a status check, the Connect a site wizard (paste a pairing code), and Sites that can connect to this one, where you create pairing codes and revoke access. Packages Export a .csync.zip for chosen pages and media or the whole site, import one by dropping it on the page, and create or restore snapshots. Advanced Publish on another site, and a danger zone with Move to recycle bin on another site and Seed another site.

Editors work from the content tree. Actions on a page or media item offer Send to…, Get from…, Add to queue and (for administrators) Publish on another site…. Each opens a side panel that ends in a review: a summary such as "4 new pages, 1 updated page", callouts for schema changes, moves and templates, and the full list behind Show details. Items always arrive as drafts. The Ferry button in the top bar opens the queue (send everything together or download it as a package) and your recent activity.

Who may send or get is set per user group with the Send with Ferry and Get with Ferry permissions, on top of the delegated-editor grants described below.

docs.title: Upgrading from CommunitySync
docs.text:
Ferry was released as CommunitySync. Upgrading is a rename, and site data is kept:

  • Packages: CommunitySync.* becomes Ferry.* (Ferry.Core, Ferry.Transport, Ferry.Umbraco, Ferry.Backoffice).
  • Code: namespaces CommunitySync.* become Ferry.*, and type and method names drop the prefix in the same way, for example AddCommunitySyncUmbracoFull() becomes AddFerryUmbracoFull() and CommunitySyncFullOptions becomes FerryFullOptions. A search and replace of CommunitySync with Ferry in your host code is enough.
  • Configuration: rename the CommunitySync section to Ferry when convenient. Until then, a site without a Ferry section keeps reading CommunitySync; a site never uses both.
  • Unchanged:
  • database tables (cmsCommunitySync*), migration state and protected connection secrets
  • the user-group permission verbs CommunitySync.Push / CommunitySync.Pull
  • the wire protocol (/community-sync/v1, transfer formats, headers), so Ferry and CommunitySync sites still transfer to each other
  • the package format (.csync.zip)

docs.title: Evidence summary
docs.text:
The current suite has 668 ordinary .NET tests and real two-site E2E suites for each module. The supported scope lists them per capability. Earlier checkpoints are recorded below.

The experimental Full v5 checkpoint had 433/433 ordinary .NET tests, a fresh exact-NuGet fixture-consumer package install using an isolated Docker SDK, a packaged Full transfer/publication run (22/22), and an exact-package two-site source-version suite with Published UploadField coverage (6/6), including native new-content SaveAndPublish, exact bytes, and unchanged replay. It also includes a culture-varying partial republish and a clean exact-NuGet two-site culture-Media Push/Pull run (2/2). SQLite and SQL Server-target runs cover the restart path. The suite asserts different en-US/fr-FR image bytes, captions, durable culture-name metadata, replay to Unchanged, and a destination process restart. These results are in ignored artifacts/ and are local evidence, not remote CI; see the validation record for paths and commands. Delegated Pull is draft-only and requires an explicit valid grant.

Earlier-package Backoffice browser evidence ran three native suites against two disposable sites in a Playwright MCP image container: 19/19 passed using the browse peer policy (artifacts/e2e/browser-snapshot-final/results.json). It predates the current production commit and covers bounded native dashboard, transfer, publication, history and remote-browse flows; it is not cross-browser, accessibility, hosted-CI, or production topology validation.

The verified subset includes invariant Content, supported Content variants and segments, selected relational MediaPicker3 references, Segment-varying scalar Media values, draft-source Content UploadField assets with hash and byte verification, and bounded Published-source Content UploadField assets captured as immutable, verified publish-time snapshots. Published export uses only the matching saved-content snapshot and fails closed when it is absent, corrupt, or does not match the published raw value. Preexisting publications without a snapshot fail closed. Native new-content SaveAndPublish captures immutable bytes before Umbraco assigns its version, then binds them to the assigned PublishedVersionId after publication. A bounded SQL Server source E2E verifies the snapshot table, primary key, and saved snapshot row. The source-version E2E also covers an en-US-only republish that preserves an untouched fr-FR immutable snapshot after its mutable file is overwritten. The current package install, source-version, and Full transfer/publication evidence is recorded in the validation record. The host sandbox still denies access to the SDK trusted-root PEM, so the clean install used an isolated Docker SDK rather than the host restore environment. Arbitrary UploadField/editor configurations, multi-node hosting, hosted CI, and cross-browser coverage are pending; unknown/custom editors and user/member references remain unsupported. This does not establish support for every Umbraco editor or parity with any commercial product. Templates must already exist at the destination; schema changes that require storage migration are blocked. Durable jobs and approval state are process-local, so multi-node operation needs affinity and external coordination. See the supported scope and acceptance checklist for exact boundaries.

docs.title: Transfer model
docs.text:
• Stable GUID identities across sites with different local numeric IDs.
  • Create/update/unchanged previews, dependency ordering and cyclic soft references.
  • Whole-site or selected-tree transfer with prerequisite/reference closure.
  • Full-mode selected exports resolve their source closure before reading content or staging media; selected preview/apply also reads only destination entities in that closure and external direct prerequisites. Adapters without scoped destination support retain full-snapshot validation.
  • Full mode optionally scopes Content variant transfer to selected cultures: it includes selected variant names and values plus invariant values, and preserves unselected destination variants. The culture scope is bound into the manifest and approval fingerprint. A Pull peer without the scoped-culture capability fails closed. Creating scoped content requires the default and mandatory cultures.
  • Selected destination fingerprints and before-state recovery records use that bounded snapshot. Incoming-entity or prerequisite edits stale the approval; unrelated destination edits do not. Shared-schema collision checks still run.
  • Peers negotiate a versioned, authenticated capability declaration before export, asset staging or destination writes. Incompatible transfer formats fail closed.
  • Preview fingerprints bound to source and destination snapshots; stale approval requires a fresh preview.
  • Native draft saves, independently of source publication state.
  • Streaming media assets are verified by SHA256 and length before application. An optional authenticated, bounded, capability-gated availability probe lets Push, Pull and the generic client skip repeat network byte transfer when the peer already has the verified staged asset. Older peers fall back to full transfer; target media is still re-exported and staged locally during planning, so this saves network bytes, not local export work. Cache eviction fails safely.
  • Full mode transfers the tested culture-varying Media shape: culture names, scalar captions, and distinct culture file descriptors. Because Umbraco 17.6.2 drops Media culture names on a fresh native read, Ferry stores approved names by Media GUID and canonical culture in its own migration-owned table. That preserves Ferry transfer semantics, but does not make the names appear in native Umbraco APIs or the Backoffice after a restart.
  • An administrator can opt in to a draft-only pull from a configured remote source, with typed roots, dependency closure, asset verification and local recovery journaling.
  • An optional, metadata-only remote Browse capability lists one bounded page of direct Content or Media children for a configured pull source.
  • An optional BrowseSearch capability finds Content or Media by name only within that same configured and authorized remote scope; it returns the same metadata-only page shape as Browse.
  • Destination-only entities are preserved. No implicit deletion or rollback.
  • Completed and potentially touched entities are reported separately on failure.

Two adapters are available. AddFerryUmbraco() supports invariant TextBox/TextArea drafts with matching preinstalled schemas. AddFerryUmbracoFull() is standalone and writes content and media through Umbraco's own services, so other packages' save handlers see Ferry's changes as normal saves. Full mode requires an ISyncAssetStore. See the documented supported editors and verified scenarios above. Existing shared data type editor/storage migrations are blocked; declared source storage is preserved. Older experimental manifests without this metadata must be re-exported.

The installed BackOffice package also has a native Umbraco composer, so its services can activate independently of Ferry's transport switch or chosen adapter.

docs.title: Host integration
docs.text:
Register the selected Umbraco adapter, then configure transport explicitly:

builder.Services.AddFerryTransport(new SyncTransportOptions
{
    BearerToken = tokenFromYourSecretProvider
});
builder.Services.AddFerryFileAssets(privateAssetDirectory);
builder.Services.AddFerryFileRecovery(privateRecoveryDirectory);
// After building/configuring the Umbraco application:
app.MapFerry();

For operation-scoped named peers, load the token through the host's secret provider and use the reload-aware registration:

builder.Configuration.AddEnvironmentVariables(); // or the host's managed secret provider
builder.Services.AddFerryTransportFromConfiguration(
    builder.Configuration.GetRequiredSection("Ferry"));

Set peer identity, revision and permitted operation names in Ferry:Peers; provide each token through the secret provider, such as Ferry__Peers__0__Tokens__0. See the peer-policy contract for the allowed operation names, reload behavior and approval lifecycle.

Supply a random bearer secret of at least 32 characters. Keep asset/recovery storage outside public static-file directories. Endpoints are disabled by default in the sample. Ferry:Mode selects DraftText (default) or Full there. No default deployment credentials are provided.

docs.title: Access keys from the backoffice only
docs.text: When Ferry.Backoffice is installed, the access keys created under Settings › Ferry › Sites (Create pairing code) are receiver credentials too. A receiver whose only credentials are those keys needs no configured token or placeholder peer: AddFerryTransportFromConfiguration (or AddFerryTransport) accepts an empty Ferry section when an ISyncManagedPeerSource is registered, and the host refuses to start when there is neither.

docs.title: Getting past host authentication
docs.text: The receiver path /community-sync/v1 authenticates every call itself (HTTPS plus a bearer token). Anything in front of it that challenges the request first - Umbraco basic auth on lower environments, an IP or SSO gateway - turns another site's call into a login page or a 401 before Ferry sees it. Let that path through: for Umbraco basic auth, add its shared-secret header (Umbraco:CMS:BasicAuth:SharedSecret) to requests on that path before UseUmbraco(), or exclude the path in the gateway.

docs.title: TLS terminated by a proxy
docs.text:
The receiver rejects plain HTTP. When TLS ends at a load balancer or container ingress (Azure Container Apps, App Service, Front Door, nginx), forward the original scheme so the request is seen as HTTPS:

builder.Services.Configure<ForwardedHeadersOptions>(options =>
{
    options.ForwardedHeaders = ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto;
    options.KnownIPNetworks.Clear(); // only when the ingress is the sole way in; otherwise list its network
    options.KnownProxies.Clear();
});
// First in the pipeline:
app.UseForwardedHeaders();

docs.title: Where state is kept
docs.text:
State Storage Survives a redeploy or new replica? Servers and access keys (backoffice) Umbraco database, tables cmsCommunitySyncServer and cmsCommunitySyncAccessKey Yes. A connections.json from 0.1.1 or earlier is imported once at startup and renamed .migrated. Secrets inside those rows Encrypted with ASP.NET Data Protection Only if the key ring is persisted and shared, for example PersistKeysToAzureBlobStorage. Otherwise keys stop authenticating after a redeploy and a warning is logged. Peer cache Memory, 30 seconds A key revoked on one instance stops authenticating on the others within 30 seconds. Operation history, durable submission mappings, snapshots and restore points Umbraco database, tables cmsCommunitySyncOperation, cmsCommunitySyncSubmission and cmsCommunitySyncSnapshot (package bytes included) Yes. The App_Data/CommunitySync folders from 0.1.1 or earlier are imported once at startup and renamed .migrated. Reviews (previews) and batch sessions Memory No. See Hosting requirements. Receiver approvals (push, publication, tree trash) Memory, keyed to the process No. See Hosting requirements. Staged assets and recovery records The directories passed to AddFerryFileAssets / AddFerryFileRecovery Only on persistent storage.

Ferry creates its tables (cmsCommunitySync*) at startup whenever its packages are installed, even when Ferry:Enabled or Ferry:Backoffice:Enabled is false. A site that only serves transfers still uses the lease table (cmsCommunitySyncLease), and the full adapter keeps media culture names and published asset snapshots in its own tables. To remove Ferry from a site completely, uninstall the packages, then drop the cmsCommunitySync* tables and delete the umbracoKeyValue rows whose key starts with CommunitySync. or Umbraco.Core.Upgrader.State+CommunitySync..

docs.title: Hosting requirements
docs.text:
Database. Use SQL Server for sites that receive transfers in production. On SQLite, a burst of writes (a large apply, for example) can deadlock Umbraco's own end-of-request cache write with its background jobs under the default Cache=Shared connection string; every later request then waits. If a site must run on SQLite, use Cache=Private in its connection string, as Ferry's own test sites do.

Previews, batch sessions and the receiver's approvals are held in process memory. A preview lasts 15 minutes (a batched push session 4 hours) and is used once. It is lost when the site restarts, scales to zero, or the apply request reaches a different instance than the preview did. Both sites in a transfer must therefore run one warm instance:

  • Azure Container Apps: minimum replicas 1 (no scale-to-zero) and maximum replicas 1.
  • App Service or other load-balanced hosts: one instance, or session affinity for the source's backoffice. The receiver must still be a single instance: site-to-site calls carry no affinity cookie.

Otherwise apply answers 410 Gone ("This preview has expired") and nothing is changed; the dashboard asks for a new preview. A receiver that loses its approval answers 410 too, and the source shows the same message.

docs.title: Protocol
docs.text:
Endpoints under /community-sync/v1 require HTTPS and bearer authentication. Responses disable caching.

Endpoint Purpose GET /capabilities Describe authenticated peer protocol, adapter, entity, operation and effective-limit support GET /manifest Export the complete supported snapshot POST /export Export selected roots, descendants and required dependencies POST /browse Return one metadata-only page of direct Content or Media children when the optional Browse reader is registered POST /browse/search Return one bounded metadata-only name-search page when BrowseSearch is explicitly granted POST /preview Validate a manifest and return a plan POST /apply Revalidate the approved fingerprint and apply GET /assets/{hash} Stream an asset PUT /assets/{hash}?length=... Verify and stage an asset GET /operations List recovery operation summaries when registered GET /operations/{id} Inspect an operation outcome GET /operations/{id}/recovery Retrieve its before-state recovery record POST /publication/preview Validate explicit destination keys and cultures POST /publication/apply Publish only the separately approved selection

Inspect SyncPlan.IsValid and ExecutionResult.Status; HTTP 200 alone does not mean an import succeeded. Authentication failures return 401, malformed requests 400, oversized requests 413 and known adapter capability errors 422. JSON defaults to an 8 MiB request limit; assets have a separate configurable limit.

SyncRemoteClient offers capability/export/preview/apply calls against one fixed HTTPS destination. SyncTransferClient.PrepareAsync() negotiates capabilities, exports a selection, stages assets and previews; ApplyAsync() is separate and rechecks the peer declaration. Redirects are disabled. Only configure trusted peers. For deployments behind a TLS proxy, configure trusted forwarded headers in the host.

docs.title: Administrator pull
docs.text:
The management API can pull a draft transfer from a configured source only when that server-side connection has AllowPull: true. POST /umbraco/management/api/v1/community-sync/pull/preview accepts a full-site choice or 1–1000 typed roots and returns an owner-bound, expiring approval. POST /umbraco/management/api/v1/community-sync/pull/{id}/apply consumes that approval, rechecks the connection and capabilities, then applies the frozen manifest through the local store and recovery journal. It neither publishes, deletes, schedules, nor re-exports remotely during apply.

Full-mode Pull can optionally scope variant data by culture. It includes names and values for selected variants plus invariant values, leaves unselected destination variants unchanged, and binds the scope into the frozen manifest and approval fingerprint. The peer must advertise the scoped-culture capability; an older Pull peer is rejected before export. Creating a culture-variant item within a scoped transfer requires the default and all mandatory cultures. The Content transfer modal exposes an optional localized culture-code input. Leaving it empty means all cultures; review displays the selected scope. Media transfer does not offer culture scope. Browser coverage verifies this bounded interaction, not broad visual, accessibility or cross-browser behavior.

POST /umbraco/management/api/v1/community-sync/pull/browse accepts a configured AllowPull source, Content or Media, an optional parent key, and page/page-size (1–100). It performs the same pull compatibility preflight as selection: source Browse and Export, local Preview and Apply, matching transfer format, and the requested kind. The source receiver itself grants Browse independently of Export, so a browse-only peer may call /community-sync/v1/browse without export access. Its response contains only key, name, a human-readable bounded breadcrumb, child presence, and cultures; it never returns properties, serialized entities, snapshots, or media bytes. A breadcrumb resolves at most the trailing 16 ancestors and begins with … if earlier ancestors were omitted.

POST /umbraco/management/api/v1/community-sync/pull/browse/search uses the same connection, authorization, compatibility and delegated-scope checks. It accepts a 2–128-character name term, rejects SQL wildcard characters (%, _, [), and returns pages of at most 50 matches with a maximum 10,000-item offset. Search is name-only: it never searches property values or serializes entities. BrowseSearch is an opt-in protocol extension (GET /capabilities?extensions=browse-search) so older capability clients do not need to parse the new operation value.

The administrator Browse API drives native Content/Media send and receive actions and a paged remote selector. Native publication selection, administrator operation history, and limited delegated editor Push are also available. Delegated Pull is available to explicitly granted groups for permitted roots and cultures, subject to native Umbraco permissions. It creates drafts only. Search and field-level differences are implemented within their documented bounds. Three native Backoffice suites passed 19/19 against two packaged disposable sites in the Playwright MCP image container, with a browse-authorized peer. Broad layout, accessibility, cross-browser and production-topology acceptance remains pending.

docs.title: Delegated editor Push
docs.text:
Administrators may grant a named Umbraco user group a limited Push to one configured destination. Add explicit grants under Ferry:Backoffice:

{
  "Ferry": {
    "Backoffice": {
      "DelegatedEditors": [
        {
          "GroupAlias": "editors",
          "Direction": "Push",
          "ConnectionId": "Production",
          "ContentRootKeys": ["11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111"],
          "MediaRootKeys": ["22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222"],
          "RemoteContentRootKeys": [],
          "RemoteMediaRootKeys": [],
          "AllowedCultures": ["en-US"]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

GroupAlias is the persisted Umbraco group alias, not its display name; ConnectionId must match the configured destination key. Local root keys are the Content and Media roots members may send, and AllowedCultures limits variant values included in the transfer. Delegated Push also checks native Umbraco Read permission and rechecks the grant and scope through preview and apply. Missing, invalid, or non-matching grants deny access by default.

Push preview keeps the legacy contentRoots array for compatible callers and also accepts roots: [{ kind: "Content" | "Media", key }]. A selected request supplies exactly one selector with 1–1000 unique nonempty keys; a full-site request accepts only the legacy empty contentRoots array. The source and destination must both advertise every selected kind before source export begins.

docs.title: Operational boundaries
docs.text:
The optional legacy receiver bearer credential grants all receiver operations. Named receiver peers can instead be limited to explicit operations and rotated tokens; their credentials and policy reload after the host publishes a new configuration snapshot, while request and asset limits stay fixed until restart. Treat every receiver credential as an administrative secret. Backoffice operator authorization is a separate layer. Fingerprints detect snapshot changes; they do not lock all CMS editors or replace authorization. The receiver serializes requests within its process; external CMS edits and multi-node writers require additional coordination.

Recovery records preserve before-state and known outcomes. They are not an atomic transaction or automatic rollback; an interrupted write can leave partial changes. Reinspect the destination and obtain a new preview before retrying. Missing outcome records mean completion is unknown. Recovery data contains site content and must be protected accordingly.

Draft content transfer does not infer publication. Schema, media, hierarchy and sort changes can affect live rendering independently of content publication. Executable templates/scripts, account replication and commercial product branding are outside scope; installed template assignments use stable keys.

See integration decisions, supported scope and recovery limits and third-party notices. Ferry is proprietary freeware (license).

docs.title: Help and feedback
docs.text:
• Bugs: open an issue with your Ferry and Umbraco versions, the database and the steps. Remove tokens, connection strings and passwords from settings and logs.
  • Questions and ideas: Discussions.
  • A package or editor Ferry should support: use the Package or editor support issue form, or add it yourself with extending Ferry.
  • Security problems: report them privately, never in a public issue.

docs.title: Completion criteria
docs.text: This tracks the implemented content-sync and separate explicit-publication scope. The experimental Full v5 checkpoint reports 433/433 ordinary .NET tests, a fresh exact-NuGet fixture-consumer package install through an isolated Docker SDK, Full transfer/publication 22/22, exact-package two-site source-version Published UploadField 6/6, and exact-NuGet culture-Media Push/Pull 2/2, including a SQL Server-target restart run. Commands and artifact paths are in the validation record. All run files live in ignored artifacts/ and are local evidence; CI evidence is pending. Checked items apply only to Umbraco 17.6.2 and the specific tested cases, not every site configuration. No commercial parity claim is made.

docs.title: Automated acceptance completed
docs.text:
• [x] Official isolated SDK; normal restore/build/test with package validation.
  • [x] Two independent real SQLite sites over loopback HTTPS with different numeric IDs.
  • [x] Draft tree transfer preserving stable keys, hierarchy, values and live versions.
  • [x] Administrator opt-in move of existing Content/Media trees. A Full destination must enable AllowExistingTreeMoves; a Push/Pull preview must explicitly request allowMoves. Preview exposes path and affected-descendant impact, binds the affected branch and publication state to approval, and stale edits reject before movement. Native moves carry destination-only descendants. The installed-package two-site Push/Pull suite passed 3/3. Native Content/Media transfer modals and Settings dashboard expose a default-off toggle and passed browser verification. Delegated moves and deletion remain unsupported.
  • [x] Receiver-only administrator tree trash of explicit Content/Media destination roots. Ferry:Full:AllowExistingTreeTrash is default-off and must be enabled; named peers need separate TrashPreview and TrashApply grants. Preview accepts 1–100 unique, non-overlapping roots and shows full subtree path, affected descendants and published descendants. It binds branch, ancestor and publication state to a one-use approval; stale state rejects before Umbraco moves the root to its native recycle bin. Recycled or top-level roots and Content branches with scheduled publication are blocked. Transfer omission never trashes, and this feature neither deletes missing items nor empties a recycle bin. The correlated journal before-state is manual recovery evidence, not automatic rollback or published-version restoration. The FINAL2 packaged Full/Full two-site trash suite passed 3/3, including Content/Media recycle-bin descendants, journal correlation, stale and replayed approval rejection, and ordinary-transfer omission (artifacts/e2e/run-fe728d8adbe5/results.json).
  • [x] Full-site Dictionary Item preview/apply preserves stable GUID identity, parent hierarchy, translations and language dependencies. This is full-site only; selected Content/Media behavior is unchanged. Moves and deletions are unsupported, and destination translation removals reject. The dictionary-item capability is opt-in, so older peers reject that kind. System audit identity is Umbraco SuperUserKey. NuGet consumer suite passed 1/1 in artifacts/e2e/run-d84b5395c2e5/results.json; package evidence is in artifacts/package-install/run-dictionary-fixed-20260924/result.json.
  • [x] Published source-version selection supports invariant and variant Full content. For variants, the current source PublishedCultures set the effective culture scope; each culture's name, template and published value transfer per segment, while drafts in unselected destination cultures persist. Selecting an unpublished source culture rejects. Full-site selection omits unpublished nodes and fails closed when an omitted unpublished ancestor is required. Draft remains the default; destination publication is separate. Peers without the version capability reject the request. Final NuGet consumer source-version suite passed 6/6 in artifacts/e2e/run-8fdee911be35/results.json, including Published UploadField same-path A/B isolation, missing-snapshot rejection before writes, and partial culture carry-forward after an en-US-only republish. Earlier-package browser suites passed 19/19 in artifacts/e2e/browser-snapshot-final/results.json; they predate the current production commit.
  • [x] Repeat import unchanged, destination-only preservation and stale approval rejection.
  • [x] Existing installed template assignments are retained when their keys match; executable template files and template hierarchies remain site code. The current exact-package Full run (22/22) includes a greenfield missing-template rejection.
  • [x] Reject scheduled target content before writes.
  • [x] Create missing languages, document/data/media types and compositions.
  • [x] Nested block dependency closure and reciprocal content references.
  • [x] Reject schema identity collisions and destructive shared data type editor changes.
  • [x] Preserve declared native data type storage; block changes requiring migration.
  • [x] Invariant/culture Content values and default/named Content segments in tested real-site scenarios.
  • [x] Full/Full relational MediaPicker3 values map to the selected destination Media identity, with unchanged repeat preview/apply (2/2 E2E cases). This does not imply support for arbitrary relational Media editors.
  • [x] Full/Full Segment-varying scalar Media TextBox values transfer with invariant values and case-varied named segments, then converge to Unchanged on repeat (1/1). Arbitrary segmented editors remain unsupported.
  • [x] Full/Full culture-varying Media for the tested name/caption/umbracoFile shape. A clean exact-NuGet two-site Push/Pull suite passed 2/2, including distinct en-US/fr-FR PNG bytes, captions, Ferry durable culture-name metadata, unchanged replay, and a fresh target process (run-d96fcf3e9db4); the SQL Server-target restart run also passed 2/2 (run-7cc1d7cd178d). Umbraco 17.6.2 natively reads these culture names as null after a fresh Media read; this proves Ferry transfer persistence, not native Backoffice display or arbitrary culture-varying Media editor support.
  • [x] Full/Full Content UploadField transfer uses hash-addressed assets and verifies exact destination bytes. Draft source covers changed source bytes and Unchanged replay. Published source is bounded to immutable publish-time snapshots: instrumented two-site source-version E2E 6/6 proves same deterministic path A/B isolation, exact Published A versus Draft B bytes, repeat Unchanged, a missing-snapshot preview rejection before target writes, and en-US-only partial republish carrying immutable fr-FR bytes forward after its live file is overwritten (artifacts/e2e/run-c7b6236be7ec/results.json). It also verifies native new-content SaveAndPublish: immutable bytes captured before VersionId=0 is assigned bind to the resulting PublishedVersionId, transfer exactly, and replay unchanged. Preexisting publications without a snapshot fail closed on Published export. Exact-package SQL Server source E2E 4/4 verifies the snapshot table, PK_cmsCommunitySyncPublishedContentAsset, and one saved row (artifacts/e2e/run-148ef4ea5e5e/results.json); SQL Server target culture-Media E2E 2/2 verifies table/PK creation with zero snapshot rows as expected (artifacts/e2e/run-923dbb295bb3/results.json). The tested culture-varying shape is limited to en-US-only republish/fr-FR snapshot carry-forward; arbitrary configurations, multi-node hosting, hosted CI, and production topology remain untested.
  • [x] Optional Full-mode culture-scoped transfer includes selected variant names/values and invariant values, preserves unselected destination variants, and binds the scope into the frozen manifest and approval fingerprint. A Pull peer without the capability fails closed; creating a scoped variant item requires the default and mandatory cultures. Full package E2E rejects a French-only create when en-US is mandatory: run-ece7838074c4. Full transfer/publication passed 21/21 and admin Pull 4/4 in preceding package run-683eb6a1e837.
  • [x] Content/media pickers, rich-text links and embedded image references.
  • [x] Media length/hash validation, native target paths and custom media metadata.
  • [x] Optional asset-availability optimization: authenticated bounded extension-gated probe verifies staged hash/length; Push, Pull and generic client skip repeat network bytes; old peers fall back to full transfer. Target media remains locally re-exported and staged during planning, so only network byte transfer is saved. Cache eviction falls back safely. Push media passed 1/1 in run-c8985f54771f and Pull passed 4/4 in run-b2324d89cce4; proxy-private counters asserted zero repeat GET/PUT transfers.
  • [x] Selected-root closure includes required ancestors, schema and referenced entities.
  • [x] In Full mode, IScopedSyncDestinationStore reads only destination entities in the dependency closure and external direct prerequisites; the same bounded snapshot drives approval fingerprints and recovery before-state. Unrelated destination edits do not stale approval, while selected-entity or prerequisite edits do. Adapters without scoped destination support retain full-snapshot behavior. Scoped E2E passed 1/1 in run-ae4d8657cce4; the recovery journal remains limited to 64 MiB per record by default and is not an atomic rollback.
  • [x] Full-mode source selection ignores unrelated invalid editors/media while selected invalid dependencies still reject; all six typed roots match full-snapshot closure.
  • [x] Authenticated peer capabilities declare the implemented protocol, adapter, entity kinds, operations and effective limits; incompatible Full/Draft formats reject before a poisoned source selection can export or write the destination.
  • [x] Named receiver peers with explicit operation scopes, rotation tokens, live policy reload after host configuration publication, and HMAC-bound expiring transfer/publication approvals. Invalid policy values fail closed before receiver I/O.
  • [x] Unsupported editor diagnostics and documented explicit adapter extension points.
  • [x] Hard dependency ordering, cyclic soft references and partial-write reporting.
  • [x] Administrative API connections, preview/apply, ownership and single-use approvals.
  • [x] Bounded optional preview names/paths from frozen Full manifests; malformed, custom or unavailable projections fall back to Kind/Key without affecting approval.
  • [x] Separate publication approval, selected cultures, ancestor validation and mandatory-language protection; publication apply rechecks enabled/destination configuration after capability negotiation; draft transfer does not infer publication.
  • [x] Ordinary tests for cancellation, recovery, limits, TLS and process-local locking.
  • [x] Opt-in durable Backoffice Push and local Pull: an administrator can select durable Push during review only when the destination advertises durable-transfer-jobs for its authenticated Apply peer. Before one bounded receiver admission POST, the Backoffice rechecks the preview's destination capability, current configuration and administrator access, then persists an owner-bound idempotency mapping. The receiver binds admission and status to that peer owner and Apply permission; same owner/key/request returns the original receipt and a changed request conflicts. The saved mapping supports receipt recovery by idempotency key and status recovery by operation ID. Lost admission/status confirmation and interrupted receiver work remain OutcomeUnknown and require destination inspection; no automatic retry, rollback, cancellation or replay is claimed. Local Pull is separately opt-in through EnableDurableLocalPull, using a separate local-Pull job kind and owner binding. At admission and worker execution it rechecks the configured source, credential, current Pull grant and native permissions. Staged Media assets are preflighted at both points, then consumed through independently verified streams; each asset is limited to 100 MiB. Its idempotency admission and receipt/status recovery are owner-bound, so it cannot cross into receiver-Apply jobs. Durable Push remains unavailable to delegated Push and publication. The latest local test totals and the packaged Media Pull, Push and Full E2E evidence are listed in the validation record; those artifact files are ignored and CI evidence is pending.
  • [x] Local NuGet consumer restore/build/publish, provenance and static assets.
  • [x] Final package's 24 Ferry App_Plugins assets byte-verified asset mounted in consumer; served import-resolution probes passed (these are not rendered-browser acceptance).
  • [x] Native publication picker/workflow and administrator operation history implemented; final-package publication/history real-site scenario passed 1/1.
  • [x] Final npm and NuGet dependency audits report zero advisories.
  • [x] Setup/scope/failure/version documentation and original/upstream license notices.

docs.title: Remaining manual/release acceptance
docs.text:
• [x] Delegated editor Push package and real-site acceptance: explicit group alias, connection, local roots, allowed cultures, native Umbraco Read authorization, and default-deny behavior. The final Dictionary-capable package passed its focused two-site suite 1/1 in artifacts/e2e/run-2c2a790f39a7/results.json, including grant revocation between preview and apply.

  • [x] Delegated editor Pull final-package scenario: explicit valid Pull grant, existing local root, permitted remote root/culture, native permission, and draft-only behavior. Full-site delegated Pull is prohibited; schema changes are denied.

  • [x] B2 administrator opt-in draft pull preview/apply final-package validation, including typed roots, dependency closure, verified assets, capability/configuration drift and recovery journaling.

  • [x] B2 bounded remote Browse metadata API real-site evidence. Configured remote roots, including nested roots, appear in a virtual paged list; delegated editors can navigate descendants after exact ancestry and direct-child checks. Prior and current-package scenarios and ordinary regressions cover separate Browse permission/capability negotiation, 1–100 direct-child pages, absent readers, revoked grants before reads, malformed remote JSON, and human breadcrumbs. Native Content/Media actions now consume Browse. The latest package also passed 2/2 dedicated Browse cases.

  • [x] Optional B2 BrowseSearch name-only metadata API. It has a distinct machine grant and opt-in capability extension, keeps Browse's local/delegated scope proofs, rejects SQL wildcard terms, limits terms to 2–128 characters, result pages to 50 and offsets to 10,000, and never searches properties or returns entity data. The latest package passed 2/2 dedicated BrowseSearch real-site cases.

  • [x] Administrator Push/Pull field comparison uses the planning snapshot and bounds supported scalar Content/Media values. Receiver Preview needs a current Export grant before target values are returned; delegated responses omit them. Ordinary authorization/projector tests and latest-package real-site Push/Pull assertions passed. The native browser suite exercised the comparison view.

  • [x] Earlier-package native Backoffice browser flows: three suites covering dashboard, transfer, publication, history and browse-authorized remote selection passed 19/19 against two disposable Umbraco sites in a Playwright MCP image container (artifacts/e2e/browser-snapshot-final/results.json).

  • [ ] Broad visual layout, accessibility, cross-browser behavior, browser lifecycle and production topology acceptance. The local container result is not hosted CI or cross-browser evidence.
  • [x] Content transfer modal optional localized culture-code input, default-all behavior, and selected-scope review verified in Docker Chromium; Media transfer does not offer culture scope.
  • [x] Final-package publication/history scenario passed 1/1; Astra re-review found no remaining P1/P2 issues.
  • [ ] Operational acceptance on the intended hosting/database/filesystem topology, with its installed custom editors, backup/restore process and concurrency policy.
  • [ ] Large-site transfer capacity beyond the documented request, manifest and BrowseSearch bounds.
  • [ ] Maintainer release review and deliberate public package publication, if desired.

Cancellation controls exist; aborting a request cannot promise rollback or prevent an already-started remote write. Recovery records report before-state and known outcomes; full site backups and host-specific restore drills remain operational work. No production service or public package is deployed automatically.

Implicit deletion, user/member replication, executable script/template deployment and commercial product branding are outside the documented scope.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to Ferry. Versions follow Semantic Versioning; while Ferry is pre-1.0, minor versions may contain breaking changes.

docs.title: Schema as generated C# migrations
docs.text:
• Generated migrations. With Ferry:Schema:Migrations enabled on a development site, schema edits in the backoffice keep a draft migration (_PendingSchemaChanges.cs, never compiled) up to date, and Create migration (Settings › Ferry › Advanced, or POST /umbraco/management/api/v1/community-sync/schema/migrations) turns it into a timestamped SchemaBuilder migration and adds it to the generated plan file FerrySchemaPlan.g.cs. The first one adopts the site's whole schema; later ones contain only what changed. See generated migrations.
  • Per-environment history. Every environment runs the listed migrations it has not run yet, in step id order, at startup. A failing migration is rolled back, blocks the later ones, and is shown on the Advanced tab and by the new Ferry schema migrations health check; the site keeps running and the next start retries it.
  • Drift. Schema changed outside the migrations (for example directly on live) is listed on the Advanced tab and by the health check until it is resolved, across deploys: a migration that changes a drifted item does not hide it. Administrators can Accept current schema (Advanced tab, or POST …/community-sync/schema/migrations/accept, all items or selected keys) to take the schema as it is there.
  • Create migration refuses while the plan lists migrations the database has not run, so a teammate's change is never undone by a diff against a database without it.
  • New SchemaBuilder steps: Remove…Async for every schema kind and for properties, groups, tabs and compositions; Rename…Async for document types, media types, templates, properties, groups and tabs; MovePropertyAsync. Removals refuse when stored values exist unless you pass allowDataLoss: true by hand.
  • .Folder(...) in Ensure… now moves an existing item into the stated folder (.Folder("") = root).
  • Files are written only in the Development environment, outside Umbraco's Production runtime mode, inside ProjectPath. Member types are not covered.
  • Sites with a hand-written 0.5 schema plan keep it running; to switch, create a first (adoption) migration and remove the old plan registration in the same commit.

docs.title: Breaking
docs.text:
• SchemaCodeExport is created through dependency injection only; its constructor is now internal. Resolve it, or ISyncSchemaCodeExport, from the container.
  • SchemaBuilder and UmbracoFullSyncStore have new optional constructor parameters. Source that calls them compiles unchanged, but code compiled against 0.5 that constructs them directly must be rebuilt (binary break).

docs.title: Behaviour changes
docs.text:
• EnsureDataTypeAsync with a stated key adopts an unused data type of the same name (re-keying it), as transfers do, instead of refusing; a namesake in use is still refused.
  • A template whose view's Layout names a plain view rather than a template is created without a master template (in SchemaBuilder and transfers), instead of failing with MasterTemplateNotFound.
  • Pages and media that no longer fit their type's root or child rules are copied where the source has them also when their type is unchanged on the destination; for media, the root and child rules are relaxed the same way as for content.
  • .Folder(...) in Ensure… moves an existing item into the stated folder; before, it applied only to new items.
  • UmbracoMediaTransfer.ValidateAsync has a new overload taking the unchanged schema items; the 0.5 overload is kept.

docs.title: Self-contained
docs.text:
• Self-contained. Ferry no longer depends on any other synchronisation package. Schema is written and read by Ferry's own serializer and importer on Umbraco's services, and property values by Ferry's own value mappers, built on Umbraco's reference tracking. Sites that also run another synchronisation tool keep working side by side.
  • Value mapper API: IFerryValueMapper and AddFerryValueMapper<T>() let you add support for your own property editors; see extending Ferry.
  • Language keys are derived from the ISO code, and built-in member property keys from the member type and alias, so every site agrees on them.
  • Transfer formats are now communitysync.full.v7 / v8. Upgrade both sites together: 0.4 and 0.5 sites refuse to exchange transfers or packages with each other.

docs.title: License and distribution
docs.text:
• Ferry is now free to use and closed source, under the Ferry Freeware License: free for any site, including commercial work; no redistribution, modification or reverse engineering. Earlier builds were never published.
  • Packages ship obfuscated, without source, symbols or repository links. scripts/release.py builds and checks them; the package E2E checks run against the same obfuscated build.

docs.title: Package data in transfers
docs.text:
• Package providers: a package can add data it keeps outside content (redirects, forms, …) to Ferry transfers by implementing IFerryPackageProvider. Items keep their keys, show in the review with their changed fields, and are written after the pages and media they point at. Off by default: set Ferry:Full:AllowPackageItemTransfer on both sites. A site without the provider refuses those items before anything is written. See extending Ferry.
  • Ferry.Skybrud.Redirects carries Skybrud redirects. Destination URLs must be site paths or http(s) URLs.
  • Ferry.Umbraco.Forms carries Umbraco Forms definitions with their workflows, and accepts the form and theme pickers. Workflow view paths must stay inside the site's views, and address settings must be public http(s) URLs.
  • Ferry:Full:AdditionalMediaExtensions allows a site's own static media types (for example .pdn). Types a browser or the server can run are refused.

docs.title: Fixes from two more real-site trials (Umbraco 17: 2,800 items with 19 redirects; 6,600 items with a form)
docs.text:
• Templates whose Layout is a plain view rather than a template transfer, including over an existing view file.
  • Pages that no longer fit their type's root or child rules copy as the source has them when the type comes along.
  • Blueprints kept in a blueprint folder no longer stop a whole-site export.
  • The display-only Umbraco.ListView property of upgraded sites is accepted.
  • Legacy {localLink:umb://…} links in rich text inside blocks no longer block the import.
  • On SQLite, Ferry's lease renewal no longer commits in the middle of an entity write, where Umbraco's relation tracking would fail with "database is locked" after retrying for minutes.
  • Legacy {localLink:1234} links by integer id approve the page they resolve to, so the import no longer refuses them as unapproved references.
  • A page whose type varies by culture but that exists in no language is left out of a whole-site export with a warning, instead of stopping it.
  • Changing a data type's editor or storage, or changing or removing a property, is allowed when no stored value uses it (a fresh site's built-in types). Element types always count as used, since block values are stored in pages.
  • Block values written in another order compare equal.
  • A peer request refused with 422 is logged with its cause on the refusing site.
  • The "would lose or change data" message shows both values as text where they differ.

docs.title: Code-first schema
docs.text:
• SchemaBuilder covers the whole schema (#30):
  • data types, with their portable configuration;
  • templates (the view file ships with the site; the layout comes from its Layout);
  • languages, media types and custom relation types;
  • document types with tabs and nested groups, folders, allowed and default templates, list views, variations, history cleanup and every property setting. Definitions are written through the same serializers transfers use, so a migration produces exactly the schema a content-only transfer compares. Nothing is removed, and destructive changes are refused.
  • Adopt code-first on an existing site (#30, #33):
  • Settings › Ferry › Advanced › Download schema as code, or GET community-sync/schema/code, writes the site's schema as one migration that keeps every key.
  • The download is a zip with one partial-class file per schema kind; format=cs returns a single file.
  • Validated on a real client site (165 document types, 463 data types): a fresh content-only install ran the migration and got 6,117 items with every schema item unchanged.

docs.title: Backoffice
docs.text:
• Spanish translation (#31). Every term the backoffice uses now has English and Spanish text, including the workspace tab labels; a test keeps it that way.
  • Accessibility checks with axe in the light and dark themes (#31); the Danger zone heading contrast is fixed.
  • Queue changes survive a reload (#32): clearing the queue and reloading at once no longer brings items back.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Real-site Get fixes (#29):
  • non-root pages kept their templates;
  • template layouts come from the Razor Layout;
  • .jfif, .jpe, .heic and .heif media are allowed;
  • orphan segment values are skipped;
  • FerryImport.IsActive lets site handlers skip work during an apply;
  • legacy block UDIs, SQL Server and SQLite dates, empty values and empty rich-text blocks no longer plan as updates.
  • Items Umbraco renamed "Name (n)" because a destination sibling holds the source name plan as unchanged (#32).
  • The packaged dashboard imported a chunk that was not committed; CI now fails when the committed backoffice build differs from a fresh one (#31).
  • SQLite: a durable apply could stall for minutes while its restore point was saved. Ferry's database work read and then wrote in one deferred transaction; when another request committed in between, SQLite refused the write (SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT), which waiting never fixes, and the provider kept retrying it. Ferry's write work now takes SQLite's write lock first, as Umbraco does.
  • The E2E fixture uses SQLite Cache=Private, which ends an intermittent Umbraco database deadlock in UI tests (#32). The README now recommends SQL Server for production sites that receive transfers.

docs.title: Renamed and standalone
docs.text:
• CommunitySync is now Ferry (#19). Packages are Ferry.Core, Ferry.Transport, Ferry.Umbraco and Ferry.Backoffice. Configuration lives under Ferry; a site with only a CommunitySync section keeps working. Database tables, routes, headers, permission verbs and file formats keep their CommunitySync names, so existing sites and peers interoperate. See Upgrading from CommunitySync in the README.
  • Standalone package (#20). Ferry has its own workspace under Settings › Synchronisation and needs no other synchronisation package.

docs.title: Backoffice redesign
docs.text:
• Send and Get replace Push and Pull throughout the interface (#21).
  • Pickers instead of GUID fields, with a key fallback for items that exist only on the other site (#21).
  • Review screen leads with a summary ("4 new pages"), calls out schema changes, moves and templates, and keeps the full list and unchanged items behind toggles (#22); the Publish review follows the same layout (#27).
  • Overview, Sites, Packages and Advanced tabs (#23): connected-site diagram, whole-site Send and Get, activity in plain sentences, a Connect a site wizard with pairing codes, drag-and-drop package import, and a danger zone for recycle-bin moves and seeding.
  • Top-bar Ferry panel with Queue and Activity tabs, and an Add to queue action (#23).
  • Side-panel buttons sit in the panel footer (#24); compact site cards, a single Synchronisation heading, and theme-aware colours (#25); Umbraco form controls, first-run guidance, a Managed in config badge and visible keyboard focus (#27).
  • Settings-tab text is translatable through ferry_* keys (#26, #27).
  • Connection checks on the Sites tab are cached for five minutes (#26).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Editors see their own activity: GET community-sync/operations/mine (#26).
  • Code-first schema: SchemaBuilder with stable, alias-derived keys (#18).
  • Content-only sites: Ferry:Full:ContentOnly rejects transfers that would change schema (#17).
  • Granular permissions on top of delegated grants (#16) and a server-side per-user transfer queue (#14).
  • Package import at startup (#12), a cluster operation lease (#11) and bulk-apply suspensions (#9).

docs.title: Fixes and maintenance
docs.text:
• Audited transitive package versions (#10) and editor reference coverage (#13).
  • The E2E harness proxy streams responses in TLS-record chunks; browser specs record failed requests (#25, #26).
  • The Settings workspace source is TypeScript.

docs.title: 0.1.0-alpha.1
docs.text: First experimental release as CommunitySync: reviewed Full-mode Push and Pull, packages, snapshots, publication, delegated editors and the native backoffice dashboard. No package was published.

docs.title: Code-first schema with SchemaBuilder
docs.text:
You can ship schema as reviewed code, run it once per environment as Umbraco migrations, and let Ferry move only content. A site that receives transfers can enforce that with Ferry:Full:ContentOnly.

SchemaBuilder covers what a content-only transfer compares:

  • data types;
  • templates;
  • media types;
  • document types, with tabs, groups, folders, templates, variations and compositions;
  • languages;
  • custom relation types between pages and media.

An existing site can adopt code-first in one step: Ferry writes its current schema as a migration that keeps every key (see Adopting an existing site).

docs.title: A migration
docs.text:
using Ferry.Umbraco.Schema;
using Umbraco.Cms.Infrastructure.Migrations;

public sealed class AddLanding(IMigrationContext context, SchemaBuilder schema) : AsyncMigrationBase(context)
{
    protected override async Task MigrateAsync()
    {
        await schema.EnsureDataTypeAsync("Tagline", "Umbraco.TextBox", dataType => dataType
            .EditorUi("Umb.PropertyEditorUi.TextBox").Config("""{ "maxChars": 80 }"""));
        await schema.EnsureTemplateAsync("landing", template => template.Name("Landing"));
        await schema.EnsureDocumentTypeAsync("landing", type => type
            .Name("Landing").Icon("icon-home").AllowedAtRoot().Folder("Pages").Composition("seo")
            .AllowTemplates("landing").DefaultTemplate("landing")
            .Tab("Content", tab => tab
                .Property("tagline", "Tagline")
                .Group("Hero", group => group.Text("heroTitle", required: true).MediaPicker("heroImage")))
            .Tab("SEO", tab => tab.Text("metaKeywords", name: "Keywords")));
        await schema.EnsureAllowedChildrenAsync("landing", "article", "landing");
    }
}

From 0.6, Ferry can write these migrations for you from the changes you make in the backoffice, and run them on every environment: see Generated migrations. You can also write them by hand and register the steps in a plan of your own that runs at startup, as for any Umbraco migration. A working example is SampleSchemaMigrationComponent in tests/e2e/FixtureSupport/FixtureSupport.cs.

var plan = new MigrationPlan("MySite.Schema")
    .From(string.Empty)
    .To<AddSeoComposition>("add-seo-composition")
    .To<AddLanding>("add-landing");
await new Upgrader(plan).ExecuteAsync(migrationPlanExecutor, coreScopeProvider, keyValueService);

SchemaBuilder is registered by AddFerryUmbracoFull().

docs.title: What the Ensure… methods do
docs.text:
Method Creates or converges EnsureDocumentTypeAsync, EnsureMediaTypeAsync Name, icon, description, folder, root and element flags, list view, variations, history cleanup, compositions, allowed templates, groups, tabs and properties EnsureAllowedChildrenAsync, EnsureAllowedMediaChildrenAsync The allowed child types, for types that allow each other EnsureDataTypeAsync Name, editor and editor UI, folder, storage, and configuration EnsureTemplateAsync The template row for a view the site ships EnsureLanguageAsync Name, default and mandatory flags, and fallback EnsureRelationTypeAsync A custom relation type between pages and/or media: name and direction. What it relates and its dependency flag are fixed once created
  • It creates the item when it is missing. When the item exists, it converges it to the definition.
  • It never removes anything. Groups, tabs and properties that a definition doesn't list are kept, so a later release restates a type with its additions only. Settings a definition leaves out keep their current value. Name, icon, description and the root and element flags are always stated; they default to the alias, icon-document (icon-picture for media types), empty and off.
  • It refuses destructive changes. These throw, because stored values could be lost: changing an existing property's data type, changing a data type's editor or storage, and changing the variations of an existing type or property. Write each of those as its own explicit migration.
  • Keys are stable. Without .Key(...), keys are RFC 4122 version 5 UUIDs derived from aliases (SchemaBuilder.StableKey): document-type:{alias}, media-type:{alias}, data-type:{name}, template:{alias}, relation-type:{alias}, {type}/group:{group alias} and {type}/property:{alias}. Every environment that runs the migration therefore has the same identities, which is what Ferry matches on, so a content-only transfer plans the schema as unchanged. .Key(existingKey) adopts an item that was created by hand. On groups, tabs and properties it also re-keys an existing one, so built-in media types on an upgraded site can be matched.
  • A data type with a stated key adopts an unused namesake. When no data type has the stated key but one with the same name exists and no property uses it (typically a fresh install's built-in, such as Content Picker, whose key differs from an upgraded site's), EnsureDataTypeAsync re-keys that data type to the stated key and converges it, as transfers do. A namesake that a property uses is refused, because its key cannot change under stored values.
  • Data type configuration is the data type's portable JSON configuration. Data types are written through the same serializers that Ferry transfers use. When the configuration is left out, an existing data type keeps its configuration.
  • Templates use the site's view file. A new template reads Views/{alias}.cshtml and never changes it. Umbraco takes its layout (master template) from the view's Layout, so create layouts first. A Layout that names a plain view rather than a template (for example Layout = "HistoryTimelineLayout.cshtml" with no such template) gives a template without a master, as Umbraco keeps one whose view was edited later, and logs a warning; renaming it or changing its name works the same way. If the view is missing, the template gets Umbraco's default view. Umbraco reads a new template's master from the view file itself, so for such a template Ferry briefly writes a placeholder into the view and then puts the original bytes back. Inside a schema migration step that write is part of the step's scope and is discarded if the step fails. Called outside a migration step (for example from your own code at runtime), there is no such scope: a crash at that moment can leave the placeholder in the view, so call the template methods from migrations.
  • Groups and tabs. Group(...) on a type is a group outside any tab. Tab(...) holds properties and groups. A group inside a tab has the alias tab/group. Use .Alias(...) when the stored alias isn't the one Umbraco derives from the name, and .SortOrder(...) when the order isn't the declaration order.
  • Properties outside any group. Sites upgraded from older Umbraco versions often have properties in no group or tab. Property(...) and the shortcuts on the type itself state such a property: type.Text("internalRemarks").Tab("Content", …). A new one is created outside every group. An existing property stays where it is, as for any property: Ensure… never moves one into or out of a group. Use MovePropertyAsync for that.
  • Property settings. Property(alias, dataTypeKey, property => …) accepts every setting:
  • Label, Describe, Mandatory (with a message), Validation (with a message), Vary, LabelOnTop, Order, Key.
  • Shortcuts use Umbraco's default data types by name:
  • Text, TextArea, RichText, Number, Toggle, Date, ContentPicker and MediaPicker.
  • For any other data type, use Property(alias, "Data type name").

docs.title: Adopting an existing site
docs.text:
A site whose schema was made in the backoffice can move to code-first without changing any key:

  1. As an administrator, open Settings › Ferry › Advanced and choose Download schema as code, or call:
GET /umbraco/management/api/v1/community-sync/schema/code?namespace=MySite.Schema&className=AdoptSchema
  • The download is a zip with one partial-class file per schema kind: AdoptSchema.cs holds the migration, and AdoptSchema.DataTypes.cs, AdoptSchema.DocumentTypes.cs and the other files hold one kind each. Large sites stay reviewable, and later diffs show which kind changed.
  • format=cs returns a single file instead.
  • Inside the application, ISyncSchemaCodeExport.GenerateFilesAsync and GenerateAsync return the same code.
  • Review the file and commit it with the site's views. Run it as the first step of the site's migration plan. Later schema changes are new migrations after it.
  • On the site it came from, it changes nothing. On a new environment it creates the same schema, so a content-only transfer from the original site plans every schema item as unchanged.

The generated migration runs in this order:

  1. Languages, relation types, data types, templates (layouts first), media types and document types (compositions first).
  2. Allowed children.
  3. Block editor configuration. Block editors name element types, so these data types are created early without their configuration and configured once the element types exist.

Settings that equal Umbraco's defaults are left out. Properties outside any group are stated on the type itself. Member types are not included; Ferry transfers them only with people.

A schema that SchemaBuilder cannot state (for example a group that contains groups, which Umbraco only allows in tabs) is refused: Create migration answers with a conflict (409) that gives the reason, and writes nothing. Change the schema in the backoffice, then try again.

This was validated on a real client site (165 document types, 463 data types, 28 templates and 9 media types):

  • A fresh content-only install ran the generated migration and pulled 6,117 items, with every schema item unchanged.
  • Running the migration again changed nothing.

docs.title: Removing, renaming and moving
docs.text:
Ensure… only adds and converges. These steps state the other changes; each is a no-op when the environment is already in the target state, so a migration is safe to run anywhere:

  • RemoveDocumentTypeAsync, RemoveMediaTypeAsync, RemoveDataTypeAsync, RemoveTemplateAsync, RemoveLanguageAsync, RemoveRelationTypeAsync, RemovePropertyAsync, RemoveGroupAsync, RemoveTabAsync, RemoveCompositionAsync.
  • RenameDocumentTypeAsync, RenameMediaTypeAsync, RenameTemplateAsync, RenamePropertyAsync, RenameGroupAsync, RenameTabAsync: a no-op when the new alias exists and the old one does not, a refusal when both exist. RenameTabAsync also renames the groups inside the tab (old/x becomes new/x).
  • MovePropertyAsync(type, property, groupAlias): an empty groupAlias moves the property out of every group and tab.

A step that would lose stored values throws, which fails the migration (Umbraco rolls the step back and Ferry reports it). The check runs on the environment that deploys, because only it knows whether content holds the values: property and composition removals use Umbraco's property usage check, asked of the type that owns each property (for a composition: the composition or nested composition that holds it, which covers every type composed of it), a data type is never removed while a property uses it, a type is not removed while content of it exists, and a language is only removed freely when no type varies by culture. Element types and a missing usage service count as "may hold values". The allowDataLoss: true parameter is for you to write by hand; Ferry never generates it.

A group or tab is only removed when it is empty (a tab: no properties and no groups). Move or remove its properties first. typeAlias resolves a document type first, then a media type.

docs.title: Generated migrations
docs.text:
You change schema in the backoffice of your development site as usual. Ferry keeps a draft migration with what changed, and Create migration turns it into a named C# migration in your project. You commit it with the code. Staging and live run every migration they have not run yet when the site starts. Nothing but the compiled C# carries schema between environments; content keeps moving with Send and Get.

Covered: data types, document types, media types, templates, languages and relation types. Member types are not covered; Ferry transfers them only with people.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Under Ferry:Schema:Migrations:

Setting Default Meaning Enabled false Run the site's generated migrations at startup and keep track of the schema they produce. Turn it on everywhere. HistoryName {SiteAssembly}.Schema Name the history is kept under, so one database can hold more than one site's history. {SiteAssembly} is the site's entry assembly name. Namespace {SiteAssembly}.Schema Namespace of the generated classes (from the assembly name, not the project's RootNamespace). WriteDrafts false Allow Ferry to write .cs files. Development only. ProjectPath none Absolute path of the web project folder (the one with the .csproj). Required for writing. Folder Migrations/Schema Folder under ProjectPath for the generated files.

On a development machine, put WriteDrafts and ProjectPath in appsettings.Development.json or user secrets:

{ "Ferry": { "Schema": { "Migrations": { "Enabled": true, "WriteDrafts": true, "ProjectPath": "/src/MySite.Web" } } } }

Ferry writes files only when all of these hold: WriteDrafts is true, the environment is Development, Umbraco's runtime mode is not Production, and ProjectPath exists and contains a .csproj. Every path stays inside ProjectPath. Otherwise nothing is written and Create migration is hidden. Staging and live never write code; they only run it.

If you change Folder, set the MSBuild property FerrySchemaFolder in your .csproj to the same value. Ferry's build files use it to keep the draft out of compilation:

<PropertyGroup><FerrySchemaFolder>Schema/Generated</FerrySchemaFolder></PropertyGroup>

docs.title: The draft
docs.text:
While writing is allowed, every schema save in the backoffice (and every folder move or rename) rewrites {Folder}/_PendingSchemaChanges.cs, a few seconds later, with only what differs from the last migration. When nothing differs, the file is deleted.

  • The draft is not compiled and not watched: dotnet watch does not restart for it, and an unfinished draft can never ship. Open it in your IDE to see what the next migration will contain.
  • Create your migration before you pull. When migrations from teammates run on your database at startup and you have a draft, Ferry first sets it aside as _PendingSchemaChanges.before-{time}.cs (also not compiled, kept as a backup) and logs a warning. Your edits are still in your database and still differ from the last migration, so after the teammates' migrations run Ferry writes the draft again with your edits in it. Where a teammate's migration restated an item you had also edited, the draft states what your database holds now; check it before you create your migration.

docs.title: Create migration
docs.text:
As an administrator, open Settings › Ferry › Advanced, enter a name such as AddLandingPage, and choose Create migration. The name becomes the class name: it starts with a capital letter and has only letters and digits. Or call:

POST /umbraco/management/api/v1/community-sync/schema/migrations
{ "name": "AddLandingPage" }

GET …/community-sync/schema/migrations/status returns the history, the draft and the drift shown on that tab.

  • Ferry writes {Folder}/{yyyyMMddHHmm}_{Name}.cs, adds it to the plan file, deletes the draft, and records the step as already applied on your database (it holds those changes already, so your next restart does not run it).
  • The first migration is the adoption migration: the whole current schema, every key kept (the same code as Adopting an existing site). Every later migration contains only the changes since the one before it.
  • The step id is {yyyyMMddHHmm}-{kebab-name}. A new step always sorts after every step already in the plan: when another migration was created in the same minute, or the plan holds a later time than your clock, Ferry moves the timestamp on a minute at a time, so migrations run everywhere in the order they were created.
  • {Folder}/FerrySchemaPlan.g.cs lists every migration with its step id. It is generated: never edit it by hand. When two branches each add a migration, git shows a conflict in it; keep both lines.
  • Create migration refuses while the plan lists migrations your database has not run (for example a teammate's migration you just pulled, or one that failed here): restart the site so it runs them, then create yours. Otherwise your migration would be a diff against a database without their changes, and would undo them wherever it runs after them.
  • Parallel branches. Two branches can each create a migration from the same starting point. Both run everywhere, in step id order. When both restate the same item (each Ensure… states the item's whole definition), the one that runs later wins and the other branch's change to that item is lost. After merging such branches, restart your development site so it runs both, check the item in the backoffice, and create one more migration if it needs fixing.

docs.title: What happens at startup
docs.text:
Ferry keeps its own history of the migrations each environment has run (not Umbraco's single "last step" state).

  • At startup, every listed migration the environment has not run yet runs, in step id order, each as an ordinary Umbraco migration in its own scope. Two branches that each added a migration both run wherever they are missing, whatever order they were merged or deployed in.
  • After a migration applies, Ferry refreshes the content type and data type caches and rebuilds the published cache once the site has started (logged as "Ferry refreshed the content type caches…").
  • A failing migration does not stop the site. The whole migration is taken back: Umbraco rolls back its database writes, the view files Umbraco wrote for its templates are discarded, and Ferry clears Umbraco's in-memory caches so nothing it created before failing is still served (a step must therefore derive from AsyncMigrationBase; the plan refuses an UnscopedAsyncMigrationBase, which Umbraco runs outside that scope). Ferry records the failure with its message, and no later migration runs until it is fixed, so they never apply out of order. The failure is logged, shown on the Advanced tab and reported by the Ferry schema migrations health check. The next start retries it. The fix is a code change: edit the failing migration and deploy again.
  • Load-balanced sites: servers in the subscriber role skip the migrations; they run on the scheduling publisher. Give every server an explicit role: register an IServerRoleAccessor that returns SchedulingPublisher on one server and Subscriber on the others (builder.SetServerRegistrar<T>(), as in Umbraco's load-balancing docs). With Umbraco's default election, every server's role is still Unknown when the migrations run at boot, so every server runs them, and two servers starting together can run the same step at once.
  • Each run logs how long it took ("Ferry schema migrations finished in … ms").

docs.title: What a generated migration contains
docs.text:
Inside MigrateAsync, the steps run in this order:

  1. Renames (types, templates, properties, tabs, groups).
  2. Property removals.
  3. Ensure… for every new or changed item, restating its whole current definition, keys included.
  4. Property moves.
  5. Group, tab and composition removals.
  6. Deletions of whole items.

Ferry checks that the steps cover every difference. Anything it cannot write safely becomes an #error Review: … line at the top of MigrateAsync, so the project does not build until you handle it and delete the line.

Changes you write by hand. These are #error lines, and Ferry does not restate the item at all; write that item's whole change yourself:

  • an existing property's data type or variation;
  • a data type's editor or storage;
  • the variations of an existing type;
  • a template's layout (master template);
  • a relation type's alias, what it relates, or its dependency flag;
  • aliases swapped or rotated between items, properties, groups or tabs;
  • a key changed while the alias stayed the same, or a container changed between group and tab.

A language's ISO code identifies it, so changing the code is written as removing the old language and adding the new one. That removal refuses wherever a type varies by culture; write the change by hand there.

Your code runs before the renames, so for a renamed item target its old alias. If the item also moved into a group that is new in this migration, create that group in your code too.

Removals and stored values. A removal refuses (and the migration fails on that environment) when stored values exist there:

  • removing a property, or a composition whose properties hold values;
  • deleting a type that has content, or a data type that any property uses (always refused);
  • element types and their properties always refuse, because block values are not tracked.

Pass allowDataLoss: true by hand when you mean it; Ferry never generates it. RemoveGroupAsync and RemoveTabAsync refuse while the group or tab still holds properties or groups, which is why removals of contents come first.

Folders. .Folder("Pages/Landing") in an Ensure… call moves an existing item into that folder (creating the folders as needed), also in the adoption migration and in migrations you write. .Folder("") moves it to the root. Without .Folder(...), the item stays where it is.

Tabs and groups. RenameTabAsync also renames the groups inside the tab. A RenameGroupAsync in the same migration that names the tab's old alias follows it.

docs.title: Drift
docs.text:
Ferry remembers the schema its migrations produced on each environment. Anything different, such as an edit made directly on live, is drift: it is listed on the Advanced tab and by the Ferry schema migrations health check, and it stays listed through later deploys until it is resolved. A deploy never hides it: when a migration changes an item that had already drifted, Ferry does not take the result as the migrations' schema, so the item stays listed (unless the migration happens to put it back exactly as the migrations had it).

To resolve drift, either:

  • make the same change on a development machine and Create migration, so every environment gets it; or
  • keep the schema as it is on this environment: as an administrator, choose Accept current schema on the Advanced tab. Ferry then treats the current schema as the migrations' schema here and the list clears. It works on any environment, including staging and live where no migration can be written. The API also accepts only some items:
POST /umbraco/management/api/v1/community-sync/schema/migrations/accept
