{ "keys": ["<item key>", "..."] }

Without keys (or with an empty list) the whole current schema is accepted. It returns the status afterwards.

On a development machine that writes drafts, nothing is listed as drift: what differs from the last migration is your draft.

Schema that arrives through a Ferry transfer is part of the migrations' schema only on a development site that writes drafts (it then shows in your draft). Anywhere else it shows as drift. Use Ferry:Full:ContentOnly on environments that receive transfers.

docs.title: Moving from a hand-written 0.5 plan
docs.text:
Sites that followed the 0.5 docs have their own MigrationPlan with an adoption migration. 0.6 leaves that plan as it is. To switch:

  1. On your development site, enable the settings above and choose Create migration. With no history and no plan file, the first migration is an adoption migration of the current schema, recorded as applied on your database.
  2. In the same commit, remove the registration of your old plan (the component or code that runs it).
  3. Deploy. Each environment runs the adoption migration once; it converges what is already there and changes nothing on a site whose schema already matches.

Ferry never reads or rewrites another plan's state.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text:
• ImageSharp advisory (GHSA-v76p-62qx-wwq2). Umbraco 17 depends on SixLabors.ImageSharp 3.1.x, which a security audit of your site reports (a heap out-of-bounds write, fixed in 3.2.0). Ferry itself does not reference ImageSharp. ImageSharp 3.2.0 refuses Release builds without a Six Labors license key, so updating it is your decision as the site owner: reference 3.2.0 directly when you have a license, or record the advisory as accepted until Umbraco moves on.

  • Set Ferry:Full:ContentOnly on every environment that receives transfers, so schema arrives only through migrations.

  • If one environment runs a newer migration than another, their schema differs, and a content-only transfer is rejected with the items to deploy first.
  • The schema-migrations E2E suite runs the sample migration on two real sites and checks the generated code: python3 scripts/e2e/run.py --mode Full --suite schema-migrations.
  • The schema-files E2E suite creates migrations on a development site, builds a release with them, runs it on a second site, and checks content-only transfers, restarts, a folder move, a property with values moved out of its group, drift and Accept current schema, and a failing removal: python3 scripts/e2e/run.py --mode Full --suite schema-files.

docs.title: Extending Ferry
docs.text:
Ferry refuses what it does not understand. A property editor it has no contract for, or data a package keeps in its own tables, blocks the transfer with a message instead of being copied half-right. This guide shows the three ways to teach Ferry about a package:

What the package adds What to do Section A property editor whose value has no ids, paths or references Declare it a scalar editor Scalar editors A property editor whose value points at pages, media or other items Register a value mapper (IFerryValueMapper) Mapped editors Data stored outside content (redirects, forms, settings rows, …) Write a Ferry package provider Package providers Media files of a type Ferry does not allow List the extension Media file types

Whatever you add, register it the same way on every site that sends or receives it.

docs.title: Scalar editors
docs.text:
A scalar value is copied exactly as stored. Use this only when the value contains no site-local ids, file paths or entity references: plain text, numbers, colours, a JSON object of settings.

builder.AddFerryUmbracoFull(options =>
{
    options.ScalarEditors.Add("Our.ColorPicker");
});

or in configuration:

"Ferry": { "Editors": { "ScalarEditors": [ "Our.ColorPicker" ] } }

If the value holds a page or media key, a scalar contract copies it without the dependency, so the page may not exist on the destination. Use a mapped editor instead.

docs.title: Mapped editors
docs.text:
A mapped editor's values are converted by a value mapper that

  • returns the value to send and the value to store on the destination;
  • reports every page and media item the value points at, so they travel with the page and the review shows them.

Keys are the same on both sites after a Ferry transfer, so a value that stores keys or umb:// UDIs can usually be copied unchanged; the mapper's job is to report the references. Ferry checks the round trip and the declared references before saving content.

Ferry includes mappers for Umbraco's own editors (pickers, Multi URL Picker, rich text, Block List, Block Grid and Single Block) and for Contentment and MetaMomentum. For your own editor, implement IFerryValueMapper (namespace Ferry.Umbraco.Values):

public sealed class LinkCardMapper : IFerryValueMapper
{
    public IReadOnlyCollection<string> Editors { get; } = ["Our.LinkCard"];

    // Keys are the same on both sites, so the stored value travels unchanged.
    public Task<string?> ToPortableAsync(object value, FerryValueContext context) => Task.FromResult(value?.ToString());
    public Task<object?> FromPortableAsync(string portable, FerryValueContext context) => Task.FromResult<object?>(portable);

    // Every page and media item the value points at.
    public Task<IReadOnlyCollection<GuidUdi>> ReferencesAsync(object value, FerryValueContext context) =>
        Task.FromResult<IReadOnlyCollection<GuidUdi>>(PageKeys(value?.ToString())
            .Select(key => new GuidUdi(Constants.UdiEntityType.Document, key)).ToArray());

    private static IEnumerable<Guid> PageKeys(string? value) => /* read the keys out of your stored JSON */ [];
}

Register it on every site that sends or receives the editor; that also opts the editor in:

builder.AddFerryValueMapper<LinkCardMapper>();

FerryValueContext.Values maps values nested inside yours, for example the properties of a block.

Declaring an alias in MappedEditors without a registered mapper does not make the editor transferable: content using it is still refused.

Test the editor on two disposable sites whose local ids differ: create content on one, Send it, and check that a second review plans it as unchanged.

docs.title: Package providers
docs.text:
Some packages keep data outside content, in their own tables: redirects, form definitions, banners, settings. A package provider lets that data travel in the same transfer as the pages and media it points at.

Ferry ships two:

Package Provider What travels Skybrud.Umbraco.Redirects Ferry.Skybrud.Redirects, builder.AddFerrySkybrudRedirects() Redirects with their root page and destination page or media. Destination URLs must be site paths or http(s) URLs. Umbraco Forms Ferry.Umbraco.Forms, builder.AddFerryUmbracoForms() Form definitions with their workflows, and the page a form goes to after submit. The form and theme pickers are accepted as plain values. Records, folders, prevalue sources and data sources are not transferred; a form that uses a prevalue or data source needs it on the destination first. 
builder.AddFerryUmbracoFull();
builder.AddFerrySkybrudRedirects();
builder.AddFerryUmbracoForms();

Forms workflows act on the server, so every workflow and field setting is checked: a view path must stay inside the site's views, and an address must be an http or https URL to a public host. Ferry checks the address as written; it cannot see what a host name resolves to when Umbraco Forms later calls it.

docs.title: Turning it on
docs.text:
Package data is off by default, because a provider writes to tables Ferry does not otherwise touch. Turn it on on both sites:

"Ferry": { "Full": { "AllowPackageItemTransfer": true } }

Each site advertises its providers. A site that receives items for a provider it does not have refuses the transfer before anything is written, with a message that names the provider.

docs.title: What a transfer does
docs.text:
• A whole-site transfer carries every item of every provider.
  • A selected transfer carries the items whose pages and media are all in the selection. An item that points at nothing, such as a form with no page after submit, travels only in a whole-site transfer.
  • Each item keeps its key on every site, shows in the review as "ItemName: name" with its changed fields, and is written after the pages and media it points at, inside the same apply.
  • An item that points at a page or media item that is missing or in the recycle bin is left out of the export and logged: it is already broken on the source.
  • Items are created or updated, never deleted.

docs.title: Writing a provider
docs.text:
Implement IFerryPackageProvider (namespace Ferry.Umbraco.Packages):

Member What it does Alias Stable id, lowercase letters, digits and dashes, for example our-banners. Never change it. ItemName What one item is called in the review, for example Banner. ExportAllAsync Every item on this site. ExportAsync(key) One item, or null. Ferry compares it with the incoming item. ValidateAsync(item) Checks an incoming item before anything is written; throw InvalidOperationException or NotSupportedException with a message for the reviewer. ApplyAsync(item) Creates or updates the item, keeping its key.

Each item is a FerryPackageItem(Key, Name, Data, References):

  • Data is a JSON object with the item's portable settings. Leave out local integer ids, dates and anything derived, so an unchanged item compares equal on both sites. Ferry sorts object properties, so field order does not matter.
  • References lists the pages (FerryReferenceKind.Document) and media (FerryReferenceKind.Media) the item needs, by key. Ferry checks they exist on the destination or come in the same transfer.
public sealed class BannerProvider(IBannerService banners) : IFerryPackageProvider
{
    public string Alias => "our-banners";
    public string ItemName => "Banner";

    public Task<IReadOnlyList<FerryPackageItem>> ExportAllAsync(CancellationToken token) =>
        Task.FromResult<IReadOnlyList<FerryPackageItem>>(banners.GetAll().Select(ToItem).ToArray());

    public Task<FerryPackageItem?> ExportAsync(Guid key, CancellationToken token) =>
        Task.FromResult(banners.Get(key) is { } banner ? ToItem(banner) : null);

    public Task ValidateAsync(FerryPackageItem item, CancellationToken token) => Task.CompletedTask;

    public Task ApplyAsync(FerryPackageItem item, CancellationToken token)
    {
        var banner = banners.Get(item.Key) ?? new Banner { Key = item.Key };
        banner.Text = (string?)item.Data["text"] ?? "";
        banner.ImageKey = (string?)item.Data["image"] is { } image ? Guid.Parse(image) : null;
        banners.Save(banner);
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }

    private static FerryPackageItem ToItem(Banner banner) => new(
        banner.Key, banner.Text,
        new JsonObject { ["text"] = banner.Text, ["image"] = banner.ImageKey?.ToString("D") },
        banner.ImageKey is { } image ? [new(FerryReferenceKind.Media, image)] : []);
}

Register it on both sites:

builder.AddFerryPackageProvider<BannerProvider>();

Guidelines:

  • Treat incoming data as untrusted. It came from another site. Validate every field in ValidateAsync and again in ApplyAsync: lengths, enums, and above all URLs (the Skybrud provider accepts only site paths and http(s) URLs).
  • Keep the key. If the package's API gives new items a random key, set the source's key after creating it (the Skybrud provider updates its row in the apply's scope).
  • Map local ids. If the package stores a page's integer id, store the key in Data and look up the local id when applying.
  • Clash with a different local item (same URL, same alias, other key): refuse it in ValidateAsync with a message that names both.
  • Payloads are limited to 256 KiB per item and 32 providers per site.

SkybrudRedirectsProvider in src/Ferry.Skybrud.Redirects is the reference implementation.

docs.title: Media file types
docs.text:
Ferry allows common image, document, audio, video and font types. To carry another static type, list it on both sites:

"Ferry": { "Full": { "AdditionalMediaExtensions": [ ".pdn" ] } }

Types a browser or the server can run (.html, .js, .svgz, .cshtml, .exe and similar) are refused at startup.

docs.title: SQLite and large transfers
docs.text: On SQLite, Umbraco's relation tracking reads and then writes after each save without taking a write lock. A commit from another connection in between, such as one of Umbraco's background jobs, which run every few seconds, fails it with "database is locked" after minutes of retries. Ferry keeps its own background writes out of that gap. For a large first transfer into a SQLite site, set Umbraco:CMS:DistributedJobs:Delay to a few hours on the receiving site for the transfer, or use SQL Server.

docs.title: Real-site validation (2026-09-28)
docs.text: Ferry was installed into a copy of a production client site and exercised between two local instances. This records what a real site exposed that the synthetic E2E fixtures did not.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Site: an agency client site on Umbraco 17.5.3 with Contentment, Block List, MetaMomentum and Google Maps editors; Azure Blob media storage.
  • Source: fresh SQL Server database seeded from the site's own schema and content export — 9,182 documents, 5,168 media, 299 document types, 496 data types, 45 templates. Media files replaced by placeholders in Azurite.
  • Target: fresh SQL Server database; schema imported from the same export (as a deployment would), content and media pushed with Ferry.
  • Installing Ferry required Umbraco 17.6.2 and EF Core 10.0.10 (the site pinned 17.5.3 / 17.0.2 / 10.0.6).
  • Driver: tests/e2e/realsite.spec.ts (COMMUNITY_SYNC_SUITE=realsite, manual only).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: Finding Fix A media record whose file is missing from Azure storage made preview return an opaque 500 (the provider throws RequestFailedException). MediaStorageFiles.Open turns any storage failure into an error naming the item; preview returns 400 with that detail. An unsupported media file (e.g. .svg) failed with no item named. The error names the item and file. Selection errors returned a generic 400 and were not logged. Logged; administrators see the detail, delegated editors keep the generic message. Dangling references blocked pushes. Content referenced deleted documents and media; 8 of 9 tried subtrees failed. Soft references to missing or recycle-bin items are skipped at the source and reported as grouped review warnings. Roots and hard dependencies still fail closed. On apply, every produced reference must still be approved; an approved one may be absent only when its target is neither in the transfer nor on the destination. Full-site push exceeded the 8 MB manifest limit (and the size check ran only after a 5-minute export). Oversized administrator pushes are split into dependency-ordered batches (at most 4 MB and 250 items each), exported once, and reviewed and applied batch by batch (preview/batches/{id}/next). One batch of 392 media updates outlived the remote client's 2-minute timeout. Batches are capped at 250 items and the remote client allows 10 minutes per request, like the asset client.

docs.title: Fixed in the follow-up round (2026-09-29)
docs.text: Finding Fix The packages pinned exactly Umbraco 17.6.2. Range [17.5.0, 18.0.0); the real site installs on its own Umbraco 17.5.3. Microsoft.OpenApi is pinned to the patched 2.9.0. Pushing schema into a fresh install collided with its built-in data types. Data types may be renamed; renames run before new data types are allocated; a name may move from a destination data type renamed in the same transfer or unused there. Apply still verifies every key. Template Razor already shipped with the site's code blocked template creation. A Views file identical to the incoming Razor is adopted. Razor is compared as Umbraco stores it (no BOM, no trailing whitespace), so adopted templates stay Unchanged. Batching spread a site's schema across batches, losing allowed child types. Schema comes first and does not count toward the 250-item batch cap. SVG media were not transferable. Static SVGs transfer after a strict safety check on export and again on the destination (no script, event handlers, foreignObject, external links or DTDs). Contentment Data List / Data Picker had to be opted in as untracked scalars. A Ferry mapper keeps the value, reports its umb:// references and exports compact JSON so repeats compare equal. Value-only editors can be opted in through Ferry:Editors:ScalarEditors. Upload autofill values (umbracoBytes etc.) made repeat pushes report Updates. Media differing only in autofilled values is Unchanged. The eye-dropper colour picker was refused. Umbraco.ColorPicker.EyeDropper and Umbraco.EmailAddress are built-in scalars. Pull and package imports kept the 8 MB limit. Bounded by Ferry:Backoffice:MaximumPackageBytes (default 256 MB); the transport request limit is not applied to local applies. A large batch exceeded the 64 MB recovery record limit. Default raised to 256 MB (a record keeps the before-state of everything a batch touches). Durable pushes could not continue batched transfers; slow sites got no guidance. 'Review next batch' after a durable job completes; interrupted applies suggest durable transfer.

docs.title: Remaining observations
docs.text:
1. Site behaviour, not Ferry: the client site's save handlers add reciprocal links (lawyers, insights, location, practices, awards) and re-sort Insights year/month folders on every save, so about 200 of ~8,500 documents differ again after each push. Its handlers also resolve nodes by production integer ids (GetById(2906)), which fails on any other database; the test copy uses the node key.
  2. Durable transfer jobs remain the answer for destinations whose saves are slower than ~2 s per item.

docs.title: Verified end to end
docs.text:
• Seed preflight: compatible v6 peers, shared Templates and Domains features, empty destination detected.
  • A real media folder (84 items): preview, apply 82/82 in 5.9 s, including recovery from an earlier apply that stopped on a storage error (restore point captured first).
  • Selected tree (Practices, 13.6 MB, 1,300+ entities with references): 8 batches, every batch previewed without errors and applied (466 content created), with unresolved-reference warnings instead of failures.
  • Full site (123 MB manifest, 15x the old limit): split into 64 batches; every batch previewed without errors and every batch with changes applied Completed — 14,105 changes including 8,380 content and 4,720 media created, with 1,301 unresolved-reference warnings. About 10 minutes of previews and 62 minutes of applies. A repeat previewed 9,011 of 9,182 documents as Unchanged; the rest are open finding 4.
  • Unauthenticated transport requests are rejected (401).
  • Fresh Umbraco 17.5.3 install, no schema import (package floor): a selected tree whose references reach most of the site (114 MB) pushed schema and content in 43 batches — 166 data types, 236 document types, 39 templates, 1,635 media and 8,426 documents. A repeat previewed all schema, templates and media and 8,289 of 8,426 documents as Unchanged (the rest is remaining observation 1).

docs.title: Second real site: a whole-site Get (2026-10-24)
docs.text: A second agency client site, an accounting firm's site upgraded from Umbraco 13, exercised Ferry 0.2.0 the other way round: a fresh install got the whole site from a copy of it.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Site: Umbraco 17.7.1 with Umbraco Forms, Umbraco Engage, Azure Blob media, Azure SSO, 2FA, Skybrud Redirects, MetaMomentum, Google Maps and Block List.
  • Source: the site's local development database (SQL Server) with 2,076 documents, 4,041 media, 165 document types, 472 data types and 28 templates. Its file export holds schema only, so the content came from the database. Media files were replaced by placeholders on local disk (the development storage account was not reachable).
  • Target: a fresh install on SQLite, with Engage removed (it refuses SQLite). The target ran POST pull/preview (fullSite: true) and pull/{id}/apply against the source over the peer protocol, so no backoffice account was needed on the source.
  • Ferry's own tables and migration keys were dropped from the source database afterwards; it matches its prior state.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: Finding Fix .jfif (22 files) and .heic were not allowed media extensions; one such file blocked the whole transfer. .jfif, .jpe, .heic and .heif are allowed static image files. A stored value whose segment the property no longer varies by (an old A/B-test variant left after an upgrade) failed the plan: Property culture/segment does not match schema variations. Export skips values Umbraco never reads (culture or segment not matching the property's variation) and logs each one on the source. A template whose Razor declares Layout = "Master.cshtml" but whose database row records no master was created before its master: MasterTemplateNotFound. Export takes the parent from the Razor layout, as Umbraco does when it creates the template; a layout that is not a template on the site is refused with a clear message. A template with no view file has empty Razor; Umbraco writes its default view on create, so the template then never matched and, being create-only, blocked every later transfer. Export sends the default view Umbraco would create. After creating a template, Ferry also checks that the stored Razor equals the approved bytes. The site's save handlers looked nodes up by production integer ids and created year/month folders on save, so the import failed on a null node. FerryImport.IsActive is true while Ferry applies a transfer; site handlers can skip work the transfer already carries. Block List values never re-saved since the upgrade from 13 (713 of 732) keep contentUdi/udi beside the keys; the import check saw contentUdi become null and blocked: Portable mapping … would lose or change data. The check treats a legacy block UDI and its key as the same block when they agree. The error now names the first differing JSON path and both values. Every page below the root lost its template on a full-site transfer: the export walked the tree with Umbraco's loadTemplates: false, and the destination snapshot used the same walk, so a repeat preview did not notice. The full-site walk loads templates. 1,685 of 2,076 pages carry a template on both sides. A repeat preview reported 1,064 of 2,076 documents as Updates although nothing had changed: dates carried a Z from SQL Server but not from SQLite, Umbraco 17 adds an empty blocks object to rich text, and an empty picker is an explicit null on one side and absent on the other. Dates are exported as wall-clock time. Content comparison uses canonical values: legacy block identities, empty rich-text blocks and empty values compare as unchanged.

docs.title: Verified end to end
docs.text:
• Preview: 6,801 operations, no errors or warnings, 77 s (export included).
  • Apply: Completed, 6,776 of 6,776 in 71 s, restore point captured.
  • Repeat preview: all documents, document types, data types, templates and 4,040 of 4,041 media Unchanged.

docs.title: Remaining observations, resolved
docs.text:
1. Duplicate sibling name. The source holds two root media folders named "Engage"; Umbraco makes sibling names unique, so the target stores the second as "Engage (1)" and each repeat planned an Update. Fixed in #32: an item that Umbraco renamed because a destination sibling holds its source name plans as unchanged.
  2. SVG media type Update. It did not recur in the code-first run below, where every media type planned as unchanged.
  3. Tables with the backoffice disabled. This is by design: the transport uses the lease table, and the full adapter has its own tables. The README explains how to remove them (#32).
  4. Code-first schema. SchemaBuilder now covers tabs, templates, variations and data types, and the site adopted code-first schema (#30). See the next section.

docs.title: Second real site: adopting code-first schema (2026-10-24)
docs.text: The same site moved its backoffice-made schema to code with SchemaBuilder.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Ferry wrote the source site's schema as one migration that keeps every key. It came to 11,600 lines:
  • 1 language;
  • 463 data types (block editors configured after their element types);
  • 28 templates, layouts first;
  • 9 media types;
  • 165 document types with 81 tabs and 129 groups, compositions first;
  • allowed children.
  • A fresh SQLite install of the same site code ran that migration at startup, with Ferry:Full:ContentOnly on, then got the whole site from the source as before.

docs.title: Fixed while adopting
docs.text: Finding Fix Templates were created in database-master order, but Umbraco takes a new template's master from its view: MasterTemplateNotFound. The generator orders templates by their views' Layout. A group named "404" has no alias Umbraco can derive (aliases cannot start with a digit). The generator writes the stored alias whenever it differs from the derived one. The site was upgraded from an old version, so its built-in media types carry legacy property keys (00000009-…); a fresh install has others, and all six built-in media types differed. An explicit key on a group or property also re-keys an existing one.

docs.title: Verified end to end
docs.text:
• The migration created every schema item on the fresh install, with no errors.
  • Content-only Get preview: no errors; all 684 schema items Unchanged (472 data types, 165 document types, 9 media types, 9 media type variations, 28 templates and 1 language).
  • Apply: Completed, 6,117 of 6,117.
  • Repeat preview: everything Unchanged except the duplicate-name media item, which #32 later fixed.
  • Running the migration a second time converged all 694 items and created nothing; the preview stayed unchanged.
  • The source database was restored to its prior state, and the trial copy was deleted.

docs.title: Real-site check: generated schema migrations (0.6.0-beta.1, 2026-10-27)
docs.text: A client site upgraded from Umbraco 13 to 17 was moved to generated migrations the way a developer would.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• On a development copy with Ferry:Schema:Migrations writing enabled, Create migration wrote the adoption migration of the whole schema, then a schema change in the backoffice became a second, change-only migration.
  • A rebuilt fresh install of the same site code, content-only, ran both migrations at startup, then got the whole site from the development copy.

docs.title: Fixed while checking
docs.text: Finding Fix Upgraded sites have properties outside every group; the adoption refused them, and the refusal surfaced as a 500. SchemaBuilder states group-less properties on the type itself, the generator writes them there, and moving a property out of every group is MovePropertyAsync(type, alias, ""). A schema Ferry cannot state is a 409 with the reason. On a fresh install the adoption failed on built-in data types whose keys differ from the upgraded site's (Content Picker). EnsureDataTypeAsync with a stated key adopts an unused namesake and re-keys it, as transfers do. A template whose Layout names a plain view (with extension) failed with MasterTemplateNotFound. Such a template is created without a master, keeping its view, also on name changes and renames. The failed step was not fully taken back: Umbraco rolled back the database, but its caches still served what the step had created, and the template views stayed. Each step runs in a scope that also covers view files; the caches are cleared when a step fails, and the failure is recorded after the rollback. Pages that no longer fit their type's root or child rules were refused when their type was already identical on the destination. They are copied where the source has them when the destination's type is the source's, including unchanged types (content and media).

docs.title: Verified end to end
docs.text:
• The rebuilt site Applied both migrations at startup, with no drift.
  • Content-only Get preview: no errors; all 330 schema items Unchanged.
  • Apply: 2,512 content and media items completed.
  • Repeat preview: everything Unchanged.
  • The development database was restored to its prior state.

Ferry is a standalone package. Full transfer saves through Umbraco's native services, so other packages' save handlers see Ferry's changes as normal saves. Its backoffice lives in Settings → Synchronisation → Ferry. Schema and media changes are applied to the destination's live definitions/files; content publication is a separate operation. Preserve a site/database backup appropriate to your hosting environment when operating on a real site.

docs.title: Selected transfers and operational limits
docs.text:
Full mode implements IScopedSyncExportStore: a nonempty root selection resolves its source closure before serializing content/schema or opening media files. Unrelated source content and media are excluded from this path. Full mode also implements IScopedSyncDestinationStore: selected preview/apply reads existing destination entities in that closure and any external direct prerequisites, without serializing unrelated destination content or media. Adapters without either optional capability retain the full snapshot path. Looking up a Language root by its portable key may enumerate serializer-derived language identities because those keys differ from native CMS language GUIDs.

Selected destination preview/apply fingerprints that bounded destination snapshot. Edits to an incoming entity or its external prerequisite invalidate approval; unrelated destination edits do not. Schema alias collisions and non-destructive shared-schema checks still run for every incoming schema during preview and again at apply. Invalid entities inside the selected source closure also continue to reject the transfer.

An optional asset-availability extension lets a peer report, through an authenticated bounded probe, whether its staging store already contains the expected hash and length. Push, Pull and generic typed clients skip repeat network GET/PUT bytes only when that capability is advertised and the staged asset verifies. Older peers receive the normal full transfer. Full descriptors remain in the manifest, approval fingerprint and recovery records. Target media is still exported and staged locally during planning; this optimization saves network bytes, not local export work. Cache eviction causes a safe full transfer.

For selected transfers, recovery records keep the before-state from the same bounded destination snapshot. The optional recovery journal remains limited to 64 MiB per record by default; it does not provide atomic rollback. Full-snapshot behavior remains for adapters that do not implement the optional scoped destination capability.

Full mode can optionally limit Content variant transfer to selected cultures. The frozen manifest carries the scope and the approval fingerprint covers it. The transfer includes selected variant names and values plus invariant values, while preserving destination variants outside the selection. A Pull peer that does not advertise this capability is rejected before export. Creating a scoped culture-variant item requires the default and all mandatory cultures. The Content transfer modal provides an optional localized culture-code input; empty means all cultures, and review shows the selected scope. Media transfer does not offer culture scope. The 12/12 browser run verifies these bounded interactions, not full UI parity.

The selected closure includes required ancestors, schemas and referenced entities. Those dependencies can be planned as updates, not only creations. Review the full plan rather than assuming that only the explicitly selected branch will change.

An administrator can opt into an existing Content or Media parent change by setting allowMoves: true on a Push or Pull preview. The Full destination must explicitly enable Ferry:Full:AllowExistingTreeMoves and advertise the negotiated existing-tree-move capability. Approval binds the move choice and target branch state; applying stale approval rejects before mutation. A native move carries the entire existing subtree, including destination-only descendants. It can affect a published path, but transfer still does not request publication. The Content/Media transfer modals and Settings dashboard expose a default-off move toggle.

Tree trash is deliberately separate from transfer reconciliation. An administrator selects one to 100 explicit, unique Content or Media roots on the destination; roots may not overlap, may not already be recycled, and may not be top-level roots. The Full destination must set Ferry:Full:AllowExistingTreeTrash to true, which is false by default. The receiver exposes separate TrashPreview and TrashApply peer-policy operations, so a peer permitted to transfer, browse, or preview another operation is not thereby permitted to trash. Delegated editor grants do not authorize tree trash.

Preview shows each selected root's path, the complete descendant impact and the number of published descendants. Its 15-minute, owner-bound, single-use approval freezes the selected branch, its ancestors and relevant publication state; a changed, missing, moved, or otherwise unsafe branch causes apply to reject as stale before a native recycle-bin move. Content with a publication schedule anywhere in the selected branch is rejected because it could publish later. The operation never infers trash from a source omission, never uses delete-missing semantics, and never empties the Umbraco recycle bin.

Before applying, the receiver records the bounded before-state in its tree-trash journal and returns the correlated operation ID with the outcome. That record supports manual investigation and host-specific recovery after cancellation, interruption or partial completion. It is not an atomic rollback and does not automatically restore prior published versions, files, or a whole site. Inspect the destination recycle bin and the correlated journal record before retrying an unknown outcome.

Peers expose an authenticated, no-store capability declaration for protocol/schema version, adapter identity, supported kinds, operations and effective limits. A transfer checks it before source export or asset staging, and rechecks it before apply. Full and DraftText use distinct transfer formats, so they cannot transfer content to one another. Publication has its own advertised operations and approval.

Source-scoped selection, bounded destination planning reads, capability negotiation and optional Full-mode culture-scoped transfer are implemented. The Content transfer modal exposes optional culture scope; Media does not. Further planning-time media optimization to avoid local re-export remains roadmap work.

Published source-version selection is a distinct Full-mode option. For variant Content, the source's current PublishedCultures determine the effective culture scope: each published culture transfers its name, template and published value for each segment. Draft values in destination cultures outside that scope persist. A selected culture that is not published at the source rejects the request. Full-site selection omits unpublished nodes and fails closed if an omitted unpublished ancestor is required by a selected published node. Draft is the default source version. A Published source version is applied as a destination draft; making it live requires the separate destination publication workflow. The version capability is negotiated before export, so peers that do not advertise it reject Published requests. Final exact-package evidence: source-version 6/6 in artifacts/e2e/run-8fdee911be35/results.json, including Published UploadField same-path A/B, repeat Unchanged, missing-snapshot fail-closed, and partial culture en-US-republish/fr-FR-snapshot-carry-forward cases; Full transfer/publication 22/22 in artifacts/e2e/run-b5b2c4780302/results.json, including the greenfield template-rejection case; fresh package install in artifacts/package-install/native-published-docker-20260925/result.json using an isolated Docker SDK. The SQL Server source proof is 4/4 in artifacts/e2e/run-148ef4ea5e5e/results.json; SQL Server target culture-Media proof is 2/2 in artifacts/e2e/run-923dbb295bb3/results.json. Earlier-package native Backoffice browser evidence passed 19/19 in artifacts/e2e/browser-snapshot-final/results.json against disposable sites in a Playwright container; it predates the current production commit. It is bounded flow evidence, not cross-browser or hosted-CI acceptance. Dictionary behavior is verified by the real API suite. Dictionary evidence: 1/1 in artifacts/e2e/run-d84b5395c2e5/results.json; package smoke in artifacts/package-install/run-dictionary-fixed-20260924/result.json. Other real-site evidence above refers to earlier packages unless an artifact is explicitly listed as current.

Boundary Current limit JSON requests 8 MiB by default; configurable up to 64 MiB Backoffice frozen transfer manifest 8 MiB Typed client manifest/ordinary JSON response 16 MiB Ordinary typed client request timeout Two minutes Adapter media export 100 MiB per file; raising transport limits does not raise this adapter limit Optional recovery journal 64 MiB per record by default; selected transfers record the bounded destination before-state, while adapters without scoped planning retain the full snapshot Optional durable job store Defaults: 16 queued/preparing jobs, 64 MiB aggregate job-record budget and 1,000 terminal records; configurable ranges are 1–64 jobs, 1–512 MiB (not below the JSON request limit), and 1–1,000 terminal records. The Backoffice admission timeout defaults to 30 seconds and is clamped to 1–120 seconds.

Source tree enumeration uses pages internally, but the transfer still builds and a whole manifest. Ordinary transfer has no paged protocol, resumable upload or background continuation. Durable Push changes only the receiver-side application step: the Backoffice saves an owner-bound idempotency/destination mapping before its one admission POST and can refresh the receipt by idempotency key or execution status by operation ID while that mapping remains accessible. Durable local Pull uses the same bounded private job store but a separate owner/job-kind binding. Its staged Media assets are preflighted before admission and again by the worker; the media consumer independently verifies the stream it opens. Each asset is limited to 100 MiB, and the job never retains bearer tokens. Both flows retain a browser session recovery key when available. A lost admission response, an unconfirmable lookup, an interrupted execution, or a restart while preparing/running yields OutcomeUnknown; inspect the destination or local site and status before creating another approved attempt. The queue never automatically retries, rolls back, cancels, resumes assets, or replays interrupted work, and it is private to one process rather than a distributed queue. These bounds are not a tested large-site capacity claim.

docs.title: Named receiver policies
docs.text:
A receiver may keep one optional legacy bearer token, which grants all receiver operations, or configure named peers with an id, rotation tokens, enabled flag, revision, and explicit operation allow-list. Named peers scope only the receiver machine credential; they do not implement user-group, content-root, or culture authorization. The available operations are capabilities, export, preview, apply, asset read, asset write, publication preview, publication apply, recovery read, browse, and BrowseSearch. BrowseSearch is absent from the default capabilities response and is advertised only when the caller explicitly requests the extension.

AddFerryTransportFromConfiguration reads named-peer policy for each request after the host publishes a configuration reload. Invalid current policy values fail closed; request and asset limits remain startup settings. An operator must advance a peer revision for every policy change. Named transfer/publication approvals are HMAC-protected, process-local envelopes that expire after 15 minutes; a restart, scale-to-zero or another instance invalidates them and apply answers 410 Gone; run one receiver instance. They are not a replay ledger or a general single-use token. See the peer-policy contract.

docs.title: User-group permissions for delegated editors
docs.text:
Ferry registers two Umbraco permission verbs, Send with Ferry (CommunitySync.Push) and Receive with Ferry (CommunitySync.Pull). Administrators assign them in the Users section, per document (granular permissions) or as a group default. Umbraco has no media granular permissions, so media transfers use the group default. A delegated editor needs the verb in addition to the configured grant and Umbraco's native permissions; the verb never replaces either. Administrators are unaffected.

Ferry:Backoffice:RequireGranularPermissions (default true) can switch the verb check off. On the first start after upgrading, every user group already configured in DelegatedEditors receives its direction's verb as a default permission, so existing grants keep working. That step runs once, so a verb an administrator later removes is never restored. Groups configured after that first start need the verb assigned in the Users section.

docs.title: Administrator pull
docs.text:
An authenticated administrator may use the management pull preview/apply API only for a configured connection whose server-side AllowPull flag is true. Preview accepts either a full site or 1–1000 typed roots, exports the source closure, stages verified assets, and freezes an owner-bound 15-minute approval. Apply consumes the approval, rechecks source/local capabilities and connection state, and writes drafts through the same local recovery journal used by receiver apply. It does not publish, delete, schedule, or create a durable job.

The optional Browse reader lists configured remote roots, including nested roots, as a virtual paged list and accepts pages of 1–100 items. It returns key, name, human-readable breadcrumb, child presence, and cultures. It resolves breadcrumb labels with one bounded public ancestor lookup per page (at most the trailing 16 IDs per item); an ellipsis marks a shortened breadcrumb. It does not expose native integer paths, properties, serialized payloads, snapshots, or media bytes. Sibling order uses native sortOrder; equal-order ties and concurrent sibling changes have no stronger pagination guarantee. A 3 MiB typed-client response ceiling bounds the largest legal escaped JSON page.

The management Browse route requires an HTTPS configured AllowPull source and the existing pull compatibility preflight: source Browse plus Export, local Preview plus Apply, matching format, and the requested kind. The source machine permission remains separate: a named peer may be granted Browse without Export. Delegated child navigation verifies remote ancestry and each returned direct child before exposing metadata. The optional BrowseSearch route repeats the same source, local, delegated and ancestry checks, then searches only entity names in the permitted Content or Media scope. Terms must be 2–128 characters, SQL wildcard characters %, _ and [ are rejected, results are metadata-only and pages contain at most 50 items; the maximum offset is 10,000. It does not query property values, serialized data, media bytes, or a general site index. Administrator previews can show bounded field differences for supported Content/Media values; delegated preview responses suppress them. Delegated Pull grants can scope permitted remote roots and cultures and must pass native permissions; they cannot request a full-site pull or schema changes. The feature remains experimental and is not production-ready.

docs.title: Explicit exclusions and fail-closed behavior
docs.text:
The tested subset is not a claim that every property editor, reference type or Media configuration transfers. Unsupported values reject before writes:

  • Culture-varying Media outside the tested name/caption/umbracoFile shape. The tested names survive through Ferry's private durable store, rather than native Umbraco's fresh Media read; arbitrary culture-varying Media editors and native Backoffice display of those names are not implied. Segment-varying scalar Media values are covered only for the tested TextBox contract.
  • Published-source Content UploadField transfer is limited to publications with a matching immutable publish-time snapshot. Missing, corrupt, preexisting, or raw-value-mismatched snapshots fail closed. New native SaveAndPublish content preserves its pre-version immutable capture and binds it only after publication assigns a matching PublishedVersionId. Draft-source transfer uses hash-addressed descriptors and exact destination-byte verification. SQL Server source validation proves the new snapshot table, primary key, and one saved snapshot row; a SQL Server target culture-Media run proves table/primary-key creation with no snapshot rows expected. The tested culture-varying shape covers an en-US-only republish carrying an untouched fr-FR snapshot forward. Arbitrary culture-varying UploadField configurations, multi-node hosting, hosted CI, production topology, and every other Content file editor remain untested.
  • Arbitrary relational Media properties/editors. The tested relational mapping is MediaPicker3 and destination Media identity; it does not imply support for every relation editor or configuration.
  • Unknown or custom editors unless the host explicitly registers and validates a scalar contract or a mapped contract with an installed mapper.
  • User and Member references. Supported references are the tested Content/Media pickers, Block List dependencies and rich-text links/images; this does not cover arbitrary relation types or every editor configuration.
  • Template files and template hierarchies, unless both peers opt into executable template transfer (see Optional modules). Otherwise a matching template must already be installed at the destination for an assignment to be retained.
  • Existing schema changes that need storage or variation migration, property removal, and composition removal. Missing compatible schemas can be created, but unsupported changes need an explicit host migration.

docs.title: Optional modules
docs.text:
These modules are off by default. Enabling any of the transfer opt-ins below moves a site to protocol/schema 2 and communitysync.full.v6; such a site negotiates only with peers that also run v6, and each manifest additionally requires the specific capability operation on both peers. Default sites keep protocol 1 and communitysync.full.v5. Evidence is from exact-package two-site runs on 2026-09-27 (artifacts/e2e/), 494 ordinary .NET tests, and client tests.

Module Enable Contract and limits E2E Executable templates Ferry:Full:AllowTemplateTransfer on both peers Create-only Razor templates as verified SHA-256 assets (1 MiB each, 16 MiB/200 per manifest); aliases [A-Za-z0-9_], _ViewStart/_ViewImports blocked; alias/key, duplicate and existing Views/*.cshtml collisions rejected (fails closed without a content root); parents created first; a stored alias or Layout-derived parent that differs from the approval is removed. Approval shows an executable-code warning. Updates, renames and deletions are unsupported; runtime rendering is not proven because the test host precompiles Razor. templates 4/4 People Ferry:Full:AllowPeopleTransfer on both peers User groups (sections, fallback and document-level granular permissions, languages, start nodes), users (groups, start nodes, language), member groups, member types and members (identity, approval on creation, groups, invariant values for text/textarea/email/integer/decimal/true-false/date editors). The Administrators group, administrators, the super-user and API users are never exported or modified; no password, security stamp, lockout, login state or token is transferred, so accounts need a password reset. Name/alias/user-name/email collisions reject before writes; other member editors and granular permission types fail the export closed; at most 10,000 members per full-site transfer. People move in full-site transfers. people 5/5 Domains Ferry:Full:AllowDomainTransfer on both peers A content node's default culture and ordered hostnames travel with the node; hostnames taken by another destination node or duplicated in one manifest reject; wildcard/unsafe names and non-BCP-47 cultures reject. Apply replaces the approved node's assignment; a node without domains never clears destination domains. domains 3/3 Offline packages Always available to administrators .csync.zip: one header (exporting site's capabilities + exact manifest) and one assets/<sha256> blob per declared asset. Import rejects unexpected names, traversal, duplicates, undeclared/missing blobs, oversize entries (MaximumPackageBytes, default 256 MiB), unsupported versions and any blob whose bytes differ from its hash, even when cached. Import uses the Pull planner, a one-time owner-bound approval and the local journal; it never publishes. Not compatible with any commercial package format. packages 3/3 Startup package import Off by default; Ferry:Backoffice:ImportOnStartup:Enabled and Files (default umbraco/Ferry/import-on-startup.csync.zip, relative to the content root) When the site starts at run level, each existing file is validated and checked for compatibility exactly as an uploaded package is. It is then planned and applied under one operation-gate hold, with the local journal, a restore point when existing entities change, and an operation-history entry (actor startup). A package whose plan has errors is never applied, and unattended import never publishes. The import finishes before the site reports started. Afterwards the file is renamed .imported or .failed and a .result.json (status, applied count, operation ID, restore point, error) is written next to it, so a restart never imports it twice. A shared file imported by several instances plans as unchanged after the first. startup-import 1/1 Snapshots and restore points Catalog always available to administrators; restore points on by default (CreateRestorePoints) Snapshots are catalogued packages (full site or roots) in the Umbraco database (cmsCommunitySyncSnapshot, shared by every instance); comparing one runs the package review against the current site, and restoring applies it. A restore point captures every destination entity an apply will touch, immediately before writing, on every local apply path: package import, snapshot restore, Pull, a Push received from another site, and durable apply; a failed capture aborts the apply (409 on the receiver). Restores write drafts and do not delete entities created after the capture, restore published versions or cover files, secrets or infrastructure. MaximumSnapshots (default 50) evicts restore points oldest-first, never manual snapshots. snapshots 4/4 Relations Ferry:Full:AllowRelationTransfer on both peers Custom relation types between Document and Media and their relations, in full-site transfers. Umbraco's system relation types (reference tracking, relate-on-copy/delete) are never transferred. A relation's identity is derived from (type, parent, child), so repeats are Unchanged and an existing identical destination relation is matched whatever its local key; relations are added or their comment updated, never deleted. Alias and object-type collisions reject. relations 2/2 Document blueprints Ferry:Full:AllowBlueprintTransfer on both peers Blueprints in full-site transfers, using the content format and the complete content apply pipeline (mapped values, references, file hashes); no parent and no allowed-at-root rule. Blueprint folders are not transferred: a blueprint kept in a folder arrives at the blueprint root. blueprints 2/2 Bulk apply suspensions On by default; Ferry:Full:BulkApply:Suspensions (None, ScheduledPublishing, Examine, DocumentCache, All) and MinimumOperations (default 50) A Full batch with at least MinimumOperations operations pauses scheduled publishing, Examine indexing and document-cache refresh through Umbraco's Suspendable switches, then resumes them once on every exit path (success, failure, cancellation). Resuming Examine after a suspended index request rebuilds all indexes, which is why small batches keep per-item indexing. Overlapping batches share one reference-counted suspension; a failing resume is logged and does not block the others. The switches are process-local, so other load-balanced instances are unaffected. Local negotiation only; no peer capability. Unit tests; packages 3/3 with MinimumOperations=1 (target log shows suspend and resume of All) Server-side transfer queue Every backoffice user with Ferry access; GET/PUT community-sync/queue Each user's queue (at most 1000 Content, Media, DocumentType, MediaType or DataType roots) is stored on the server in cmsCommunitySyncQueue, one row per user, created by its own CommunitySync.TransferQueue migration plan. The queue follows the user across browsers and is cleared after a completed transfer as before. The browser keeps a synchronous cache: the server copy replaces it when the backoffice loads, a browser queue from before is uploaded once, and a server without the endpoint keeps the browser-only queue. Queued Content and Media show a "Queued for transfer" sign in trees and collections (CommunitySync.QueuedForTransfer flag); the sign appears when the tree is next loaded. Queueing grants nothing: every transfer is still authorized at review. queue 1/1 Content-only sites Off by default; Ferry:Full:ContentOnly on the receiving site For sites whose schema is deployed with the code, for example code-first migrations or schema files in source control. Any Push, Pull, package or startup import whose plan would create, update or move a document, media or member type, data type, language, template, media-type variation or relation type is rejected before anything is written. The error lists up to 20 items (kind, alias, key) to deploy first. Unchanged schema prerequisites are accepted, so content whose types already match transfers normally. A page or media item that no longer fits its type's root or child rules (Umbraco checks them only when an editor creates or moves it) is copied where the source has it when the source's type is in the transfer, including when that type is unchanged. The check runs on every planned transfer, at review and again at apply. Dictionary items, members and other content-like kinds are not affected. content-only 2/2 Code-first schema (SchemaBuilder) Use SchemaBuilder in your own Umbraco migrations; see code-first schema Ensure… methods create or converge data types, templates, languages, media types and document types (tabs, groups, folders, templates, variations) and never remove anything. Destructive changes (a property's data type, a data type's editor or storage, variations) are refused. Keys are RFC 4122 v5 UUIDs derived from aliases, so every environment gets identical identities and content-only transfers plan the schema as unchanged. Remove…Async, Rename…Async and MovePropertyAsync state removals (refused while stored values exist, unless allowDataLoss: true is written by hand), renames and moves into or out of groups. GET …/community-sync/schema/code writes an existing site's schema as one migration that keeps every key. schema-migrations 6/6 Generated schema migrations Off by default; Ferry:Schema:Migrations:Enabled everywhere, plus WriteDrafts and ProjectPath on development machines; see generated migrations Backoffice schema edits keep a draft migration; Create migration writes a timestamped SchemaBuilder migration and the plan file (the first one adopts the whole schema). Every environment runs the migrations it has not run, in step id order, at startup; a failing one is rolled back with its template views, blocks later ones and is reported on the Advanced tab and by a health check. Drift from the migrations is listed across deploys until resolved or accepted (Accept current schema). Member types are not covered. Verified on a real upgraded site: adoption plus a change migration applied on a rebuilt site, all 330 schema items Unchanged on Get, 2,512 items applied. schema-files 5/5 Package data Off by default; Ferry:Full:AllowPackageItemTransfer on both peers, plus a provider registered on both (AddFerrySkybrudRedirects(), AddFerryUmbracoForms() or your own AddFerryPackageProvider<T>()) Items a package keeps outside content, as PackageItem entities with their keys. A whole-site transfer carries every item; a selected transfer carries the items whose pages and media are all selected. Items pointing at missing or binned pages or media are left out of the export and logged. Items are created or updated, never deleted. Peers negotiate provider aliases; a missing provider refuses the transfer before anything is written. Skybrud redirects: destination URLs must be site paths or http(s). Umbraco Forms: definitions and workflows; records, folders, prevalue and data sources are not transferred, and a form whose prevalue or data source is missing on the destination is refused. See extending Ferry. package-items 4/4 Site seed Administrators seed/preflight reports compatibility, destination emptiness (when Browse is granted) and shared optional features; the seed is the ordinary full-site Push review, so re-running re-plans and applies only remaining differences. seed 3/3

docs.title: Schema storage and migrations
docs.text:
Where schema is deployed with the code, set Ferry:Full:ContentOnly on the receiving site so transfers carry content only (see the modules table).

Data type exports declare native storage metadata. Apply preserves that declared storage instead of normalizing to the editor's default storage. Existing shared data type editor or storage changes are blocked before mutation because they can affect destination-only content, unless Umbraco reports that no stored value uses the data type (for example a fresh site's built-in types); a data type used by an element type always counts as used. The same applies to changing or removing a property. Property removal, storage/variation changes, composition removal and other unsupported schema migrations require an explicit migration. Older experimental manifests without storage metadata must be exported again with the current version.

docs.title: Custom property editors
docs.text:
Unknown custom editors fail closed. Declare verified behavior explicitly:

umbraco.AddFerryUmbracoFull(options =>
{
    options.ScalarEditors.Add("Custom.PlainText");
    options.MappedEditors.Add("Custom.Relations");
});

Use a scalar contract only for values that contain no site-local IDs, file paths or entity references. A mapped contract additionally requires an installed value mapper for the editor. The adapter checks mapped round trips and declared references before saving content; declaring an alias does not create a mapper automatically. Validate your custom editor on two disposable sites with different local IDs.

docs.title: Explicit publication
docs.text:
Publication selects destination content keys and cultures, obtains a fresh publication preview, then requires its fingerprint in a separate apply request. A sole * explicitly requests every currently available culture; invariant content also uses *. Specific culture selections remain specific. An unpublished ancestor must be explicitly selected where supported or published separately. An invariant child beneath an unpublished culture-variant ancestor requires that ancestor to be published first. Publication schedules must be handled separately.

The service validates properties and checks current draft/schema/ancestor and language configuration state. Missing mandatory cultures must already be published or explicitly selected; they are never silently added. It does not infer source publication, publish unselected ancestors, unpublish, change schedules or perform an automatic rollback. Completed items stay published if a later item fails. OutcomeUnknown means a native call may have changed that item before throwing; inspect its state before obtaining a new preview.

docs.title: Recovery and concurrency
docs.text:
The optional journal writes the selected destination draft before-state (or the full snapshot for adapters without scoped planning), attempted operation and approved fingerprint before mutation, followed by an independent outcome. A missing outcome means completion is unknown. Publication recovery contains draft state, not a copy of every previous published version; it cannot reverse publication. Assets referenced by recovery records must remain in the configured asset store. Retention and site/database backups remain host responsibilities.

One operation gate covers the following:

  • inbound sync
  • backoffice source export and planning
  • Pull, package and snapshot apply
  • durable jobs

Where the backoffice package is installed, the gate also holds a cluster-wide lease while each operation runs. The lease is a single cmsCommunitySyncLease row in the Umbraco database, so instances that share the database run one Ferry operation at a time. The lease works as follows:

  • An instance claims it with a conditional update and renews it every 30 seconds.
  • Claiming waits until the lease is free. If the caller's request is canceled, it gives up without taking the lease.
  • An instance that stops without releasing the lease loses it after two minutes.
  • Expiry uses each instance's UTC clock, so keep instance clocks synchronized.

A receiver-only host without the backoffice package keeps the process-local gate.

Preview fingerprints reject changes before application. Neither safeguard locks external CMS editors or other writers for the entire operation. Use appropriate operational coordination for actively edited sites.

There is no implicit deletion, account replication, executable template/script deployment, or guarantee that every third-party editor works without an adapter.

docs.text: Documentation reviewed on 2026-09-17. Some older /extending and /reference documentation links now redirect or return a suggested replacement path.

docs.title: Package layout and registration
docs.text:
Umbraco recommends NuGet distribution and keeping a package library, tests and an example website in the repository. Ferry follows that layout with an explicit .NET 10 / Umbraco 17.6.2 adapter project. Shared package metadata marks the code under the Ferry Freeware License (free to use, closed source).

The opt-in AddFerryUmbraco() extension registers the constrained text store through IUmbracoBuilder.Services. It does not enable network endpoints or install a credential. The example website registers the transport separately and maps its endpoints only when Ferry:Enabled is true. This avoids changing installed sites merely because they reference the library. Scoped store instances allow the adapter to use request-scoped Umbraco dependencies without a singleton capturing them.

AddFerryUmbracoFull() opts into the staged schema/language/content/media adapter. Referencing the package alone does not select this adapter. The backoffice package adds the Ferry workspace under Settings › Synchronisation (Overview, Sites, Packages and Advanced tabs), Send/Get actions and a top-bar queue for editors, and a Management API; enable it with Ferry:Backoffice:Enabled and configure named HTTPS destinations on the server. Neither destination credentials nor transfer payloads are sent to the browser. The workspace's generated client uses the Umbraco 17.6 authentication context and native refresh/interceptor configuration.

Sources: Creating a Package, Example Package Repository, Dependency Injection, Composing.

docs.title: Draft persistence
docs.text:
The initial adapter uses IContentService.Save, not a generic import pipeline. It never calls publication, unpublication or schedule-writing methods. The native save result is checked. Existing target items with schedules are blocked because their changed draft could otherwise be published by a future scheduled operation.

The pinned service implementation has a separate save path and accepts a nullable schedule argument. Keeping schedule changes out of the payload is intentional. This does not promise zero live-site impact: sort order and later schema/media changes may affect rendering independently of content publication.

Historical API research used Umbraco 17.3.2 ContentService. The build and tests now target 17.6.2; that historical source link is not a compatibility claim for all 17.x versions.

docs.title: Current capability boundary
docs.text:
The constrained adapter remains available for invariant text properties on existing matching document/data types. The optional full adapter implements staged schema and language transfer, variant draft content, mapper-based references and media support. Those implementations are distinct from acceptance: real-site fixture results and explicit editor coverage determine what can be claimed as working. Template code, arbitrary custom editors and unsupported tree operations must not be silently dropped. Check current adapter validation and the verification record before deployment.

Both preview and apply run the adapter's whole-manifest preflight before any writes. Preflight checks are repeated at write boundaries. Backoffice source export shares the transport operation gate for snapshot and local asset staging, then releases it before remote requests. Process-local serialization and these checks are not a distributed transaction: external editors or another application node can still race the operation. Real database integration and locking must be established before a production release.

See the example website for an explicitly scoped acceptance fixture and verification for tests actually executed.

docs.title: Implemented receiver contract
docs.text:
The receiver can authorize either an optional legacy BearerToken or named peers. A named peer has a stable Id, one to eight rotation Tokens, an Enabled flag, a Revision, and an explicit list of allowed operations. The allowed names are Capabilities, Export, Preview, Apply, AssetRead, AssetWrite, PublicationPreview, PublicationApply, and RecoveryRead. An empty list grants no receiver operation.

The optional legacy token remains available for existing deployments and grants all receiver operations. A named peer is the appropriate choice when a receiver needs separate machine identities or operation scopes. This is receiver authorization only: it does not grant Umbraco user-group, content-root, or culture permissions.

Use the host's secret provider and register the configuration section directly. For example, the host may populate Ferry__Peers__0__Tokens__0 through its secret-provider integration before the application is built:

builder.Configuration.AddEnvironmentVariables(); // or the host's managed secret provider
builder.Services.AddFerryTransportFromConfiguration(
    builder.Configuration.GetRequiredSection("Ferry"));

The corresponding non-secret configuration can contain peer identity and scope:

{
  "Ferry": {
    "Peers": [
      {
        "Id": "deployment-agent",
        "Enabled": true,
        "Revision": "2026-09-17",
        "AllowedOperations": [ "Capabilities", "Export", "Preview", "Apply" ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

Do not put a token value in source-controlled configuration. Each peer object accepts only Id, Tokens, Enabled, AllowedOperations, and Revision; unknown fields, invalid operation names, comma-combined names, numeric enum values, and malformed scalar/list shapes are rejected. Startup rejects invalid configuration. With AddFerryTransportFromConfiguration, peer policy is read for each request after the host has published a configuration reload. An invalid current policy value fails closed and a corrected published configuration takes effect on the next request. This does not detect a configuration-source parse failure or a missed host reload notification; those are host configuration concerns. Request and asset limits remain startup values; peer credentials and permissions, including the optional legacy bearer token, are live-reloaded.

Every HTTPS request that reaches receiver authentication sends Cache-Control: no-store. A missing, unknown, disabled, or revoked token returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer. A recognized peer without the requested operation returns 403. Protected work reauthorizes after it enters the receiver's operation gate and before it reads a snapshot, starts a journal record, publishes, or writes. A queued request therefore observes permission or token revocation before it can access receiver state.

docs.title: Capabilities and approvals
docs.text:
Named peers receive the adapter declaration intersected with their allowed operations. Asset read and asset write are independently represented; a legacy combined asset capability is expanded only into directions the named peer is allowed to use. The capability response includes a non-secret policy fingerprint and its approval-token limit. Legacy peers retain the existing adapter declaration.

For named peers, transfer and publication previews return an opaque approval envelope instead of the raw planner or publisher fingerprint. The envelope binds the raw fingerprint to the peer id, the canonical hash of its id/revision/operations, the purpose (transfer or publication), and a 15-minute expiry. It is protected by an HMAC-SHA256 key generated for the receiver process. Apply validates the current peer, policy hash, purpose, expiry, and MAC before any journal, store, publisher, or write access. Bad or stale envelopes return 410 Gone ProblemDetails ("This approval has expired"); a policy denial remains 403. Legacy peers continue to use raw approval fingerprints.

The approval key is process-local. Restarting the receiver invalidates named-peer approvals. Multi-node deployments need preview/apply affinity until a durable shared approval protector exists. Envelopes are not single-use and do not provide a replay ledger; the existing backoffice prepared-transfer store retains its separate single-use behavior. Token rotation that preserves id, revision, and operations retains an unexpired envelope. Operators must advance Revision for every policy change: restoring the same id, revision, and operation set can make an unexpired envelope valid again.

The additional capability fields can cause strict older clients to reject a new receiver declaration. Upgrade both peers when adopting named policies; this is deliberately fail-closed rather than a claim of wire compatibility with older strict clients.

docs.text: The ordinary .NET suite currently has 191 passing tests: 74 Transport, 42 Core, 8 Backoffice, and 67 Umbraco adapter. The peer-policy coverage includes strict startup and reload binding, exact expiry, queued permission and token revocation, envelope purpose and policy-drift rejection before I/O, and directional asset capabilities. The current real-site E2E set has 30 scenarios: 19 final-package consumer cases, 4 named-policy cases, 4 coexistence cases, 1 scoped-export case, and 2 legacy-capability cases. Their run records and scope are in verification.
